title: Storage spike & data-tier wiring (QuestDB / Parquet+DuckDB / Postgres)
body:
## Context
CandleViewer stores three incompatible workloads: a tick/L2 firehose (~0.5-0.75 GB/day/symbol compressed at 200 depth), a long-lived archive for replay and analytics, and strongly relational, transactional OMS/auth/audit state. `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0003-storage-tiers.md` locks a three-tier answer (QuestDB hot, Parquet+DuckDB cold, Postgres 16 relational) **and** makes that answer conditional: spike S2 (`docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §15) must benchmark QuestDB against TimescaleDB on the *real* query shapes before the choice is hard-committed, with TimescaleDB named as the designated fallback.

This epic is the R0 answer to that gate plus the minimum data-tier wiring every later epic builds on. `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §4.2 scopes E07 as: "QuestDB vs TimescaleDB benchmarked on the real query shapes (footprint cell aggregation over a session, replay scan of one symbol-day of L2 deltas, CVD time-series roll-up); Parquet cold-tier layout + DuckDB query path; Postgres schema bootstrap + Alembic; retention job skeleton; **ADR-0008 hot-tier selection**" at 26 pts across S02-S03. R0 exit criteria #3 and #6 (`§4.3`) depend directly on it: ADR-0008 merged with measured numbers, and "ticks, L2 deltas and 1-minute bars for those symbols are readable from QuestDB and archivable to Parquet; a DuckDB query returns one symbol-day".

The binding structural rule from ADR-0003 is what makes the decision reversible and is therefore the most important deliverable of this epic: **all storage access goes through repository interfaces in `services/api/candleviewer/storage/` (module M10, `CONSTITUTION.md` §3). No module issues SQL or ILP directly.**

Plan material:
- `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0003-storage-tiers.md` (tier table, reversal path, validation via spikes S2 and S6).
- `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §4 (QuestDB DDL, dedup, partitioning, operational notes), §5 (Parquet layout, file-format rules, export job, compaction, DuckDB views, tier-routing rule), §6 (lifecycle hot->cold, pinning, disk pressure), §7 (retention matrix), §8 (backup/restore), §9 (Alembic rules, revision plan 0001-0013), §11 (sizing + throughput budget), §13 (access patterns -> index rationale).
- `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §2 (containers), §6.2 (start order `storage -> auth -> ... -> gateway`), §12 (storage metrics `questdb_write_seconds`, `pg_pool_in_use`, `pg_query_seconds`), §14 (risk: "QuestDB does not meet real query shapes"), §15 spike S2.
- `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §5.8 Area 8 (S1-S6) and SR-047, SR-048, SR-090..SR-099.
- `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` budgets #12 (storage growth) and §6 (ingestion/memory/storage).
- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §4 (fixtures), §5 (integration via docker compose / testcontainers with QuestDB + Postgres), §6 (soak).
- `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` line on the hot-tier risk.

## Scope / Deliverables (children)
| Key | Kind | Title | Pts |
|---|---|---|---|
| E07-K01 | Spike | QuestDB vs TimescaleDB on the three real query shapes | 5 |
| E07-T01 | Task | M10 `storage` package: repository interfaces, AppContext wiring, fakes | 2 |
| E07-T02 | Task | Postgres bootstrap: SQLAlchemy metadata, Alembic 0001/0002, CI migration gates | 5 |
| E07-T03 | Task | QuestDB tier: DDL runner, ILP writer, PGWire reader, repository impls | 5 |
| E07-T04 | Task | Parquet cold tier: exporter, manifest/checksums, DuckDB views | 5 |
| E07-T05 | Task | Retention/archive job skeleton + `source_tier=auto` query router | 3 |
| E07-T06 | Task | ADR-0008 hot-tier selection + doc reconciliation | 1 |
| E07-D01 | Task | Design: operator content model + `StorageUsage` contract review (feeds E16-D04) | 3 |
| E07-D02 | Task | Contract QA: shipped E07-T05 `StorageUsage` payload vs the operator content model | 2 |
| E07-Q01 | Task | QA: black-box test plan + storage contract/integration suite | 3 |
| E07-Q02 | Task | QA: exploratory charter - tier boundary, dedup, backfill idempotency | 2 |
| E07-Q03 | Task | QA: storage perf/load harness (ILP ingest, query shapes, export) | 3 |
| E07-Q04 | Task | QA: chaos - DB down, disk full, crash between export and drop | 3 |
| E07-X01 | Task | Security: STRIDE threat model for recorder data & storage (Area 8) | 3 |
| E07-X02 | Task | Security: control verification SR-047/048/090-099 + SAST/DAST rules | 3 |

**Epic `estimate` = 26**, matching the E07 budget in `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §3 (epic table) and §4.2 (train scope line, S02-S03).

**Sizing convention (explicit, so this is not read as a rollup error):** the Epic `estimate` field carries the *engineering* budget only - the Spike/Story/Task children (`K`/`S`/`T` keys) that consume delivery-team velocity in the roadmap train. Here that is K01 5 + T01 2 + T02 5 + T03 5 + T04 5 + T05 3 + T06 1 = **26**, exactly the roadmap figure. The design (D), QA (Q) and security (X) children are *discipline tracks* sized and scheduled on their own capacity lines (Design 5, QA 11, Security 6; all-children arithmetic sum 48) and are deliberately **not** added into the epic estimate, because `30-release-roadmap.md` §3/§4.2 budgets trains in engineering points. A naive 48 would double-count discipline capacity against the R0 train and make E07 look ~85 % larger than the roadmap commitment.

Roadmap reconciliation: roadmap E07 = 26 pts; epic `estimate` = 26 pts; engineering-child rollup = 26 pts. ✓

## Out of scope
- The recorder itself (recorded-symbol list, auto-record triggers, disk-budget UI behaviour) - **E16** (M11).
- The replay engine and its seek/scrub semantics - **E26** (M12).
- The order-flow derived tables' *producers* (footprint/profile/CVD engines) - E18/E19/E23. E07 creates the tables and the write path; it does not compute the values.
- OMS/auth/audit business logic - E09, E27, E29. E07 creates the Alembic revisions listed in §9.4 only up to the point each owning epic needs; revisions `0003`+ are authored by their owning epics using the conventions E07 establishes.
- **Any user-facing screen.** E07 has **no FE/UI Story children and ships no screen**. `SCR-142` (Admin: storage & database panel) is designed by **E16-D04** (Sprint 05), design-QA'd by **E16-D07** (Sprint 09), implemented by **E16-S04** (Sprint 08) and a11y-audited by **E16-Q05**. E07 owns only the *data contract* behind it (`GET /api/v1/recording/storage`, schema `StorageUsage`, emitted by E07-T05), the operator content model that constrains that contract (E07-D01) and the verification that the shipped payload satisfies it (E07-D02). No Figma screen, no React code, and no design-ahead obligation is carried by E07.
- Backup automation and restore drills as an operational cadence - E43/PRR; E07 documents the procedure and proves one manual restore.
- Any second exchange, Android client, or public-internet exposure.

## Acceptance criteria (epic level)
```gherkin
Given a clean WSL Ubuntu host running `make up`
When the backend boots
Then the M10 storage module reports healthy for all three tiers and the supervisor start order places storage first, per 20-architecture.md §6.2

Given one recorded symbol-day of real Bybit BTCUSDT data
When the three benchmark query shapes from 21-database-schema.md §13.2 (#2 footprint aggregation, #7 replay seek + delta scan, #8 CVD roll-up) are run against both QuestDB and TimescaleDB
Then p50/p95/p99 for each shape on each engine are recorded in ADR-0008 and a decision is stated with the measured numbers attached, not opinions

Given trades, orderbook_deltas and bars_time rows written through the repository interfaces
When the nightly export job runs and then the retention reaper runs
Then Parquet files exist under the §5.1 layout with SHA-256 manifest entries, row counts match the source exactly, and only then are the QuestDB partitions dropped

Given the export job is killed between writing Parquet and dropping the hot partition
When it is restarted
Then the run completes with duplicate-but-consistent data and zero missing rows, proving the ordering invariant of §5.3

Given a DuckDB session against cold/analytics.duckdb
When `SELECT count(*) FROM trades WHERE symbol='BTCUSDT' AND dt='2026-11-10'` is issued
Then one symbol-day is returned within the §13.3 budget and the row count equals the pre-export QuestDB count

Given an `import-linter` contract run in CI
When any module other than M10 imports asyncpg, psycopg, duckdb, pyarrow or the ILP client
Then the build fails, enforcing the ADR-0003 repository rule
```

## Technical notes / design
Tier assignment is fixed by ADR-0003 and must not be re-litigated inside child tickets; the only open question is hot-engine identity, answered by E07-K01/E07-T06. Repository interfaces are Python `Protocol`s in `services/api/candleviewer/storage/repositories/`, with three implementation families: `questdb/` (ILP write + PGWire read), `postgres/` (SQLAlchemy 2.0 async), `cold/` (pyarrow + DuckDB). Each repository has an in-memory fake used by every other module's unit tests, which is what keeps the rest of the codebase engine-agnostic.

Time is integer microseconds UTC everywhere (`20-architecture.md` §3 conventions); QuestDB's designated timestamp is always the exchange event time, `recv_ts` is never designated. Every QuestDB table is WAL-enabled with `DEDUP UPSERT KEYS` so reconnect/backfill replays are idempotent - this is a correctness requirement, not an optimisation, because E08's resubscribe-on-gap path re-delivers rows.

Config keys (M1 `config`, `24-internal-schemas.md` §ParquetConfig / RetentionConfig): `CV_QUESTDB_ILP_HOST/PORT`, `CV_QUESTDB_PG_DSN`, `CV_PG_DSN`, `CV_COLD_ROOT`, `CV_RECORDER_HOT_DAYS` (default 7), `CV_RECORDER_RETENTION_DAYS` (default 30), `CV_PARQUET_COMPRESSION` (zstd:6), `CV_PARQUET_ROWGROUP_MB` (128), `CV_STORAGE_MIN_FREE_PCT` (15).

Error codes surfaced by M10: `STORAGE_TIER_UNAVAILABLE`, `STORAGE_EXPORT_VERIFY_FAILED`, `STORAGE_SCHEMA_DRIFT`, `STORAGE_RETENTION_BLOCKED_BY_PIN`, `STORAGE_DISK_CRITICAL`.

## Test plan
Rolled up from children: unit (repository fakes, manifest/checksum logic, router boundary maths) >=85% line coverage on `services/api/candleviewer/storage/`; contract tests asserting every repository Protocol is satisfied by both the real and the fake implementation; integration via `docker-compose.test.yml` (QuestDB + Postgres + MinIO) driven by recorded Bybit fixtures from `packages/fixtures`; perf harness for the three query shapes plus ILP ingest rate; chaos for DB-down and disk-full; one manual restore drill.

## Security notes
Data classifications A-10 (recorded market data), A-13 (backups) from `04-security-program.md` §3. Threats S1 (silent Parquet corruption), S2 (disk exhaustion takes trading down - **Critical**), S3 (path traversal via dataset ids), S5 (retention deletes pinned data), S6 (QuestDB/DuckDB console exposed). Controls: SR-094 checksum manifest + weekly scrub, SR-096 separate volume + 75%/90% guards, SR-097 registry-addressed datasets with zero user-supplied paths, SR-099 pin-honouring dry-run-first retention with audited deletions, SR-047/SR-048 loopback-only binds and unpublished data-store ports. Epic carries the `security` label; STRIDE model is E07-X01 and must be Done before E07-T05 merges.

## Accessibility notes
Backend epic; the one UI surface it designs is SCR-142 (E07-D01/E07-D02) - per-tier tables with units on every figure, health communicated as text not colour alone, WCAG 2.2 AA per `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`.

## Performance notes
Budgets: `21-database-schema.md` §11.4 - QuestDB ILP ingest >=600k rows/s, Parquet export >=200 MB/s, DuckDB replay scan >=1 GB/s from page cache, Postgres OMS <=50 tx/s. Query-shape targets from §13.2/§13.3. Storage growth budget #12 (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md`): 0.75 GB/day/symbol is the provisioning figure; E07 instruments the real number so E16 can replace the estimate.

## Observability
`questdb_write_seconds`, `questdb_ilp_rows_total`, `pg_pool_in_use`, `pg_query_seconds`, `storage_export_rows_total{stream,result}`, `storage_export_duration_seconds`, `storage_retention_dropped_bytes_total{symbol,stream}`, `storage_disk_free_ratio{volume}`; `system_events` rows for export verify failures (CRITICAL) and retention runs; audit entries for every deletion (symbol, stream, range, bytes) per SR-099.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All children Done or explicitly descoped with a recorded disposition.
- [ ] ADR-0008 merged with measured p50/p95/p99 per query shape per engine; ADR-0003 amended if the fallback is taken.
- [ ] R0 exit criteria #3 and #6 demonstrably satisfied in a demo.
- [ ] Coverage >=85% on `services/api/candleviewer/storage/`.
- [ ] `import-linter` contract forbidding direct DB drivers outside M10 is green in CI.
- [ ] STRIDE model (E07-X01) finalised, findings triaged, Security engineer sign-off comment.
- [ ] QA sign-off recorded (E07-Q01..Q04 executed).
- [ ] Design sign-off (CDO) on the **operator content model** (E07-D01) plus Architect sign-off on E07-D02's verification that the shipped `StorageUsage` payload satisfies it. (No screen sign-off: E07 ships no UI; SCR-142 hi-fi sign-off belongs to E16-D04.)
- [ ] `21-database-schema.md` §14 open-to-verify items updated with measured values.
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review with the storage panel data payload and a DuckDB symbol-day query.

## Dependencies
- **E02** (monorepo scaffold): needs `services/api` module tree M1-M24, `import-linter` harness and the docker compose stack with postgres + questdb + minio (`E02-T05`, `E02-T08`).
- **E03** (CI/CD): migration job with single-head check and the `integration` gate that starts the compose stack.
- **E04** (observability): Prometheus scrape target for the storage metrics this epic emits.
- Downstream consumers: **E12** (bars & series), **E16** (recorder, retention & disk budget - consumes the E07-D01/D02 content model and frozen payload fixture as the input to E16-D04's SCR-142 design and E16-S04's implementation), and through them E18/E19/E23/E26 - see `30-release-roadmap.md` §11.1 edges `E07 --> E12` and `E07 --> E16`.

## Branch
`feat/storage-tier-*` per child (e.g. `feat/storage-tier-questdb`); PR size <=400 LOC; migration PRs require the `backend/db/**` code-owner approval per `21-database-schema.md` §9.3 rule 13.

## Agent guidance

How to pick up work in this epic when multiple agents are running in parallel:

**Dependency order.** Work tickets in `blocked_by` order; a ticket is not pickable until every key in its `blocked_by` list is Done. Design (`-D*`) and spike (`-K*`) tickets generally gate the technical (`-T*`) and story (`-S*`) tickets that consume their output — check each ticket's `blocked_by` field, do not assume numeric order implies dependency order.

**Parallel lanes.** Tickets with disjoint `component` values and no shared `blocked_by` edge can run concurrently: backend (`api`/`data-feeds`) tickets, frontend (`web`) tickets and design (`-D*`) tickets form separate lanes once their own upstream design/contract tickets are Done. QA (`-Q*`) and security (`-X*`) tickets typically depend on the corresponding `-S*`/`-T*` ticket being Done, so they are the last lane per feature slice, not a separate epic-wide phase.

**Shared interfaces to agree first.** Before two agents touch the same contract (API/WS schema, DB table, or statechart) concurrently, the one opening the PR first must land the contract change (OpenAPI/WS schema/migration) and regenerate `packages/protocol`; the second agent rebases on it rather than proposing a second incompatible shape. Statechart JSON under `machines/` is single-owner per PR — check open PRs touching the same `machines/<name>.machine.json` before starting a `statechart`-labelled ticket.

title: Spike: benchmark QuestDB vs TimescaleDB on the three real CandleViewer query shapes
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0003-storage-tiers.md` chose QuestDB as the hot tier but explicitly conditioned it: "Vendor benchmark claims are disputed (a ClickHouse maintainer's rebuttal showed indexed ClickHouse beating QuestDB on disk by ~3x), so the choice must be reversible", and its Validation section names **spike S2**: "run the real footprint, profile, CVD and replay-scan queries against both QuestDB and TimescaleDB on a week of recorded BTCUSDT/ETHUSDT data; record p95 per query shape". `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §15 lists S2 with the decision criterion "Query suite p95 documented for both", and §14 lists the matching architectural risk. `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §4.1 goal 3 makes this one of the two decisions R0 exists to retire, with §4.5 putting **ADR-0008 merged by 2026-11-06**.

This spike answers the question; E07-T06 writes the ADR.

## Question to answer (precise)
For CandleViewer's actual workload - 2-5 USDT perp symbols at 200 depth, single box (4 vCPU / 8 GB VPS profile per `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §3) - does QuestDB 8.x meet the per-shape latency targets in `21-database-schema.md` §13.2 by a wider margin than TimescaleDB (PG16 + timescaledb 2.x), when both hold the same week of recorded data?

## Timebox and decision criteria
- **Timebox: 6 working days**, agreed with the Architect. Not extendable without an Architect note on the ticket.
- **Decision rule, stated up front:** QuestDB is confirmed if it meets *all* target latencies in the table below at p95 and is not worse than TimescaleDB by more than 25% on any shape. If QuestDB misses any target that TimescaleDB meets, the ADR-0003 reversal path is taken (hot tier moves to TimescaleDB, collapsing hot+relational) and ADR-0003 is amended, not superseded. If **both** miss a target, the spike is extended by 2 days to test the tuning levers in §4.14 before any decision.
- Explicitly **not** production code: prototype lives on `spike/storage-hot-tier` and is left unmerged.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A loader that ingests one week of recorded `BTCUSDT` + `ETHUSDT` fixtures (`packages/fixtures`, `03-testing-strategy.md` §4.1) into (a) QuestDB 8.x via ILP and (b) TimescaleDB hypertables, using the identical logical schema of `21-database-schema.md` §4 (`trades`, `orderbook_deltas`, `orderbook_snapshots`, `bars_time`, `footprint_cells`, `orderflow_metrics`).
- Benchmark harness `spikes/storage/bench.py` running each shape 30x warm + 5x cold-cache, reporting p50/p95/p99 and bytes scanned.
- The three roadmap-mandated shapes plus three supporting ones:

| # | Shape (from `21-database-schema.md` §13.2) | Target |
|---|---|---|
| A | Footprint cell aggregation over a session: `footprint_cells WHERE symbol AND bar_family AND bar_param AND ts BETWEEN` (500 bars) | < 150 ms |
| B | Replay scan of one symbol-day: nearest `orderbook_snapshots ... ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 1` then forward `orderbook_deltas` scan | < 200 ms seek, then sustained scan |
| C | CVD roll-up: `orderflow_metrics WHERE symbol AND ts BETWEEN SAMPLE BY $interval` | < 60 ms |
| D | Chart bootstrap: `bars_time` 100k bars | < 100 ms |
| E | Big-trade scan: `trades WHERE notional > x AND ts BETWEEN` | < 80 ms |
| F | Last price: `tickers LATEST ON ts PARTITION BY symbol` | < 10 ms |

- Ingest-side measurement: sustained ILP rows/s vs TimescaleDB COPY rows/s against the §11.4 target (>=600k rows/s QuestDB).
- On-disk size per engine after the same week (this is where the disputed claim lives).
- Operational comparison table: backup/restore mechanics, retention primitive (`DROP PARTITION` vs `drop_chunks`), out-of-order handling, dedup/idempotency, ops surface (one daemon vs two).
- A portability check: confirm the §4 table shapes use no QuestDB-only types beyond `SYMBOL`, and record the exact TimescaleDB equivalent DDL so the reversal path is a known quantity.
- Findings written to `docs/plan/spikes/S2-hot-tier.md` with raw numbers and the harness command line.

## Out of scope
- ClickHouse (ADR-0003 rejected it for single-box operations; re-opening it needs a new ADR).
- Production repository implementations - E07-T03.
- Writing the ADR - E07-T06 (this spike supplies the evidence).
- Multi-node / clustered configurations.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given one week of recorded BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT fixtures
When the loader runs against a fresh QuestDB and a fresh TimescaleDB on the reference VPS-profile container limits
Then both engines hold identical row counts per table, verified by a count assertion per table, before any query is timed

Given both engines loaded
When the benchmark harness runs shapes A-F
Then a results table with p50/p95/p99 per shape per engine plus bytes-scanned and on-disk size is committed to docs/plan/spikes/S2-hot-tier.md

Given a shape where QuestDB misses its target while TimescaleDB meets it
When the decision rule is applied
Then the spike concludes "take the ADR-0003 reversal path" and files the follow-up tickets for the TimescaleDB repository implementation, rather than leaving the decision open

Given out-of-order fixture delivery (a reconnect replaying 30 s of already-ingested rows)
When both engines ingest it
Then QuestDB's DEDUP UPSERT KEYS and the TimescaleDB unique-index-upsert equivalent both yield the original row count, and any divergence is recorded as a correctness finding that outranks latency

Given the timebox expires with shapes unmeasured
When the spike is reviewed
Then it closes with a partial-evidence ADR entry ("defer, need more data" is itself an ADR outcome per 02-definition-of-ready-done.md §5.2) and a named follow-up, never silently rolls over
```

## Technical notes / design
Run both engines in the compose stack from `E02-T08` with CPU/memory limits matching the VPS profile (4 vCPU / 8 GB) so numbers are transferable, not workstation-flattered. QuestDB config per `21-database-schema.md` §4.14: `o3MaxLag=300s`, `maxUncommittedRows=500000`, explicit `SYMBOL CAPACITY`, WAL on, ILP batched at 5000 rows / 100 ms. TimescaleDB side: hypertables chunked to match QuestDB partition granularity (1 day for `trades`, 1 hour for `orderbook_deltas`), `timescaledb.compress` on chunks older than 1 day with `segmentby=symbol, orderby=ts`, and a unique index on the dedup key for upsert parity.

Cold-cache runs must drop the page cache between iterations (container restart or `echo 3 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches` on the host) - otherwise every result measures RAM, not the engine. Report both, labelled.

Measure the *client-observed* latency through PGWire/asyncpg, not the engine's internal timer, because that is what M10 will experience.

Pseudo-code for the harness core:
```python
for engine in (questdb, timescale):
    for shape in SHAPES:
        for mode in ("warm", "cold"):
            samples = [time_query(engine, shape.sql, shape.params) for _ in range(shape.n(mode))]
            record(engine, shape.id, mode, p50(samples), p95(samples), p99(samples))
```

## Test plan
The spike's own correctness gates: row-count parity per table after load; a golden-result assertion that each shape returns *identical result sets* on both engines (sorted, float-compared with 1e-9 tolerance) - a faster engine returning different numbers is a failed spike, not a win; harness self-test on a 1000-row synthetic set so a broken timer is caught before the real run.

## Security notes
Fixtures only - no real credentials, no live exchange connection (`03-testing-strategy.md` §5 "no network egress"). Both engines bind loopback only in the spike compose file per SR-047; the QuestDB HTTP console must not be published to the host (SR-048), even in a spike, because spike compose files get copied.

## Accessibility notes

title: Create M10 storage package: repository Protocols, AppContext wiring, in-memory fakes, import-linter contract
body:
## Context
ADR-0003 states the binding structural rule that makes the whole storage decision reversible: "**all storage access goes through repository interfaces** in `services/api/candleviewer/storage/`. No module issues SQL or ILP directly. This is what makes the hot tier swappable." `CONSTITUTION.md` §3 defines module **M10 `storage`** (`services/api/storage/`, depends only on M1 `config`) as the owner of "Postgres repositories, QuestDB writer/reader, Parquet/DuckDB tier, retention". `20-architecture.md` §3 fixes the module package layout (`__init__.py` exporting only the public interface, `service.py` lifecycle, `models.py` pydantic v2 types, `errors.py`) and §6.2 puts `storage` **first** in the supervisor start order.

This task builds that contract surface before any engine-specific code exists, so E07-T02/T03/T04 are implementations behind it and every other module can be written and unit-tested against fakes from day one.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `services/api/candleviewer/storage/__init__.py` exporting only: the repository Protocols, `StorageService`, domain models, error types.
- `storage/service.py` implementing the lifecycle contract `async start(ctx: AppContext)`, `async stop(grace_s: float)`, `health() -> HealthReport`, opening/closing the three tier clients and reporting per-tier health.
- `storage/models.py` (pydantic v2): `TimeRange` (integer microseconds UTC), `SymbolStream`, `StreamKind` (`trades | orderbook_delta | orderbook_snapshot | tickers | klines | liquidations | open_interest | funding_rates | bars | footprint_cells | profiles | orderflow_metrics | heatmap_cells`, aligned with `22-api-openapi.yaml` `StreamKind` and `21-database-schema.md` §4), `TierHint` (`hot | cold | auto`), `ExportRun`, `RetentionDecision`.
- `storage/errors.py`: `StorageTierUnavailable`, `StorageExportVerifyFailed`, `StorageSchemaDrift`, `StorageRetentionBlockedByPin`, `StorageDiskCritical` - each with a stable string code used in logs and `system_events`.
- `storage/repositories/` Protocols:
  - `MarketDataRepository` - `write_trades`, `write_book_deltas`, `write_book_snapshot`, `write_tickers`, `write_bars`, `read_bars`, `read_trades`, `read_book_snapshot_at`, `read_book_deltas`, `read_orderflow_metrics`, `read_footprint_cells`, `latest_ticker`.
  - `RelationalRepository` factory exposing per-aggregate repositories (`UserRepository`, `AuditRepository`, ... created by their owning epics; E07 ships the base `UnitOfWork` and session management only).
  - `ColdTierRepository` - `export_partition`, `list_manifest`, `query` (DuckDB), `verify_checksums`.
  - `RetentionRepository` - `policies()`, `plan(dry_run: bool)`, `apply(plan)`.
- In-memory fakes for every Protocol in `storage/testing/fakes.py`, shipped as part of the package's public test surface so other modules import them (`from candleviewer.storage.testing import FakeMarketDataRepository`).
- `AppContext` wiring in `services/api/candleviewer/app.py`: storage clients constructed once and injected (`20-architecture.md` §6.1 - "No module constructs its own dependencies").
- `import-linter` contract in the repo config (extending `E02-T06`): forbidden imports of `asyncpg`, `psycopg`, `sqlalchemy`, `duckdb`, `pyarrow`, `questdb` from any package other than `candleviewer.storage.*` and `backend.db.*`.

## Out of scope
- Any real engine client (E07-T02 Postgres, E07-T03 QuestDB, E07-T04 cold tier).
- Aggregate-specific relational repositories (owned by E09/E27/E29 etc.).
- Retention *logic* - E07-T05 (this task defines only the Protocol).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given the storage package with only fakes registered
When the app supervisor boots with CV_STORAGE_BACKEND=fake
Then storage starts first, health() reports all three tiers as "fake/healthy", and the app reaches SelfCheck without any database container running

Given a module outside M10
When it adds `import asyncpg` and CI runs
Then the import-linter contract fails the build with a message naming ADR-0003

Given FakeMarketDataRepository
When a contract test suite written once is parametrized over [fake] today and [questdb, timescale] later
Then the same suite passes unchanged, proving the Protocol is engine-agnostic

Given storage.stop(grace_s=5) is called while a write is in flight
When the grace window elapses
Then in-flight writes are awaited or cancelled deterministically, connections are closed, and no "Event loop is closed" warning is emitted

Given a tier client fails to connect at boot
When health() is called
Then it returns degraded for that tier with the StorageTierUnavailable code, and the supervisor refuses readiness rather than serving with a silently missing tier
```

## Technical notes / design
Protocols, not ABCs, so implementations need no inheritance and fakes stay trivial:
```python
class MarketDataRepository(Protocol):
    async def write_trades(self, rows: Sequence[TradeRow]) -> None: ...
    async def read_bars(self, sym: str, family: BarFamily, param: str,
                        rng: TimeRange, tier: TierHint = "auto") -> list[BarRow]: ...
    async def read_book_snapshot_at(self, sym: str, ts_us: int,
                                    depth: int) -> BookSnapshotRow | None: ...
```
Every read method takes `TierHint`; the `auto` resolution lives in E07-T05's router, not in call sites. Write methods are batch-only (`Sequence[...]`) on purpose - a per-row API would make the ILP batching budget of §4.14 unreachable.

`HealthReport` per tier: `{tier, state: ok|degraded|down, latency_ms, detail}`. Readiness (`/readyz`, E04) requires `postgres=ok`; `questdb` degraded is allowed to serve reads-from-cold but must surface on the health screen; `cold` degraded blocks export only.

Config is read exclusively from M1 (`24-internal-schemas.md` §3195 `ParquetConfig` and siblings). The package must not call `os.environ` directly - checked by a unit test.

## Test plan
- Unit: Protocol conformance test (`typing.runtime_checkable` + a structural assertion per implementation), fake behaviour (round-trip write/read, range filtering, ordering by `ts`, dedup on natural key), error-code stability test (a frozen mapping of exception class -> string code, so log consumers do not break silently), lifecycle test (start/stop idempotency, stop during in-flight write).
- Contract: the shared repository suite that E07-T02/T03/T04 must each pass - authored here, executed there.
- Integration: app boots with fakes and no containers.
- Coverage target: >=90% on this package (it is small and interface-dense).

## Security notes
No credentials handled here beyond passing DSNs from M1; DSNs are `SecretStr` and `__repr__` must never render them (SR-006/SR-007 secret type wrapper, SR-120..SR-124 logging redaction). A unit test asserts `repr(settings.pg_dsn)` contains no password substring. The import-linter contract is itself a security control: it is what keeps SQL construction in one reviewed place, limiting injection surface.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no UI.

## Performance notes
Interface shape is a performance decision: batch-only writes, `TierHint` on reads, and returning `list[Row]` of pydantic-lite dataclasses (not ORM entities) for market data, because §13.2 targets (<100 ms for 100k bars) cannot absorb ORM hydration. Market-data rows use `msgspec.Struct`/slots dataclasses, not pydantic models, on the read path - benchmark recorded in the PR.

## Observability
Registers the metric names the implementations will populate: `questdb_write_seconds`, `questdb_ilp_rows_total`, `pg_pool_in_use`, `pg_query_seconds`, `storage_tier_health{tier}` (`20-architecture.md` §12). Structured log context keys `tier`, `stream`, `symbol`.

- [ ] AC verified by tests; coverage >=90% on the package.
- [ ] `import-linter` contract merged and demonstrated failing on a deliberate violation (screenshot/CI link in the PR).

title: Bootstrap Postgres relational tier: SQLAlchemy metadata, Alembic 0001/0002, naming conventions and CI migration gates
body:
## Context
Postgres 16 is the relational tier of ADR-0003 and the system of record for users, roles, sessions, keys, profiles, OMS state, journal and the hash-chained audit log. `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §9 defines the migration regime in full - Alembic 1.13+ over SQLAlchemy 2.0 Core metadata with `asyncpg`, a **single linear history** (`alembic heads` must return exactly one revision, enforced in CI), reversible `downgrade()` exercised by CI, `CONCURRENTLY` index builds, expand->migrate->contract for breaking changes, a 60 s per-migration timing budget, and a pinned `migrations/lockfile.json`. §9.4 lists revisions `0001_initial` through `0013_partitioning`.

E07 owns the *regime and the foundation*: the cluster/role setup (§1.1), enum types (§1.2), shared domains (§1.3), trigger functions (§1.4), revision `0001_initial` (extensions, domains, enums, triggers, `users`, `roles`, `permissions`, `role_permissions`, `user_roles`, `sessions`, `sessions_rotation`, `mfa_*`, `recovery_codes`) and `0002_rbac_seed`. Every later epic authors its own revisions (`0003`+) using these conventions. E03's pipeline supplies the migration job; this ticket supplies what that job runs and the checks it enforces.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `backend/db/models.py` - SQLAlchemy 2.0 `MetaData` with the §9.3 rule-12 `NAMING_CONVENTION` (`ix_`, `ux_`, `ck_`, `fk_`, `pk_`), the source of truth for autogenerate.
- Cluster/role bootstrap per §1.1: database `candleviewer`, roles `cv_owner` (DDL, runs migrations), `cv_app` (DML only, **no DDL privileges**), `cv_ro` (read-only, used by the DuckDB `postgres` attachment in §5.5). Idempotent script `infra/scripts/pg_bootstrap.sql`.
- Extensions, PG enum types (§1.2 - including `retention_action` referenced by `22-api-openapi.yaml` `x-db-enum`), shared domains (§1.3), and the shared trigger functions (§1.4, incl. `set_updated_at`).
- `backend/db/alembic.ini`, `migrations/env.py` (async engine, `compare_type=True`, `compare_server_default=True`), `migrations/versions/0001_initial.py`, `0002_rbac_seed.py`, `migrations/lockfile.json`.
- `backend/db/seeds/roles_permissions.yaml` and the bootstrap-owner seed (§10.2) consumed by `0002_rbac_seed`.
- `SqlAlchemyUnitOfWork` implementing the `RelationalRepository` session/transaction surface from E07-T01: async session factory, explicit transaction boundaries, `pg_pool_in_use` / `pg_query_seconds` instrumentation, statement timeout and `application_name` per connection.
- CI gates (jobs contributed to E03's workflow): `alembic heads` single-head check; `upgrade head -> downgrade -1 -> upgrade head` on a scratch DB; autogenerate-drift check (`alembic check` must report no diff between `models.py` and head); migration timing budget (<60 s against the seeded volume fixture); lockfile integrity (editing an applied revision fails).
- `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §9.4 table annotated with "landed in E07-T02" for 0001/0002.

## Out of scope
- Revisions `0003_exchange_accounts` onward - authored by their owning epics (E27, E29, E16, E35, E40, E41, E42) using these conventions.
- Auth/RBAC business logic and the audit hash-chain trigger - **E09** (this task creates the `users`/`roles`/`sessions`/`mfa_*` *tables*; `audit_log` and its chain trigger are revision `0012`, owned by E09/E42).
- QuestDB and cold-tier schema - E07-T03/T04.
- `order_events` monthly partitioning (revision `0013`) - E29.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given a freshly created empty Postgres 16 database
When `alembic upgrade head` runs as cv_owner
Then revisions 0001 and 0002 apply, `alembic heads` returns exactly one revision, and the elapsed time is under 60 seconds

Given head is applied
When `alembic downgrade -1` then `alembic upgrade head` runs on the same database
Then both succeed and a schema dump before and after is byte-identical modulo timestamps, proving downgrade() is real and not a stub

Given the cv_app role
When it attempts `CREATE TABLE`, `ALTER TABLE` or `DROP TABLE`
Then Postgres refuses with insufficient_privilege, asserted by an integration test

Given a developer adds a column to models.py without generating a revision
When the autogenerate-drift CI check runs
Then the build fails naming the drifted table and column

Given a migration file that has already been applied is edited
When CI validates migrations/lockfile.json
Then the build fails with the 21-database-schema.md §9.3 rule-9 message "migrations are forward-only in production"

Given the seed in 0002_rbac_seed is applied twice
When the migration is re-run on a database that already has the seed
Then it is idempotent (no duplicate rows, no constraint violation)

Given an index is added on a table declared to exceed 1M rows
When the revision is reviewed in CI
Then a lint asserts it uses CONCURRENTLY and the revision sets transactional = False
```

## Technical notes / design
Async engine with `asyncpg`; `poolclass` sized for the VPS profile (`pool_size=10, max_overflow=5`) because §11.4 budgets Postgres at <=50 tx/s - a large pool is wasted memory here. Every session sets `SET LOCAL statement_timeout = '30s'` and `application_name = 'candleviewer:<module>'` so slow queries are attributable on the SCR-142 panel.

`env.py` must run migrations through a **sync** connection obtained via `connection.run_sync` (Alembic's async recipe) and must set `version_table_schema='public'`, `include_schemas=False`. Enum handling is hand-written per §9.3 rule 6 - `ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE` cannot run in a transaction block, so such revisions set `transactional = False`; enum value *removal* is forbidden (rule 7).

Seed loading reads the YAML files and performs `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` keyed on the natural key, which is what makes rule-5 idempotency true.

The `UnitOfWork` exposes exactly one commit point per request/command; nested `begin()` uses savepoints. Repositories never commit - only the UoW does. This is the invariant E29's OMS depends on for "no order is acknowledged before it is durably recorded".

## Test plan
- Unit: naming-convention generation (assert produced constraint names match the template for a synthetic table); UoW commit/rollback/savepoint semantics against an in-memory SQLite-async stand-in for fast cases plus real PG for the rest; seed idempotency.
- Integration (testcontainers-python, `03-testing-strategy.md` §5): full upgrade/downgrade/upgrade cycle; role privilege matrix (`cv_owner` / `cv_app` / `cv_ro` x DDL/DML/SELECT); statement-timeout enforcement; pool metrics populated.
- Contract: `RelationalRepository`/UoW conformance suite from E07-T01.
- Perf: migration timing against a seeded volume fixture; `pg_query_seconds` histogram sane under a 50 tx/s write loop.
- Coverage target: >=85% on `backend/db/`.

## Security notes
- Least privilege is the control: `cv_app` holds no DDL, `cv_ro` is the only role the DuckDB attachment uses (§5.5 `ATTACH ... READ_ONLY`), preventing analytics paths from mutating the ledger.
- DSNs and passwords are `SecretStr`, never logged (SR-120..SR-124); the bootstrap script takes them from the environment, never from a committed file; `.env.example` carries `CHANGE_ME` placeholders only.
- Postgres binds loopback/compose-internal only and its port is not published to the host or tailnet (SR-047, SR-048) - asserted by the `infra/scripts` bind check from `E02-T08`.
- `21-database-schema.md` §12 classifies columns; `users` carries PII and `mfa_*` carries secret material, so this revision is reviewed by the Security engineer even though it ships no auth logic. Label `security` set for that reason.
- Migration PRs additionally require the `backend/db/**` code-owner approval (§9.3 rule 13).

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no UI.

## Performance notes
Budget: Postgres OMS writes <=50 tx/s (§11.4); migration <=60 s (§9.3 rule 11). Index rationale for these tables is §13.1. No `CONCURRENTLY` needed on 0001 (empty database) - the lint applies from `0003` onward.

## Observability
`pg_pool_in_use` (gauge), `pg_query_seconds` (histogram, labelled by `application_name` suffix), `pg_migration_version` (gauge with the numeric head), `pg_migration_pending` (gauge, drives the SCR-142 "migration pending" banner). A `system_events` row on every migration apply with the from/to revision.

## Context
The hot tier serves every chart, footprint, profile and recent-replay read in the product; `21-database-schema.md` §13.2 lists twelve query shapes with targets from <10 ms (last price) to <200 ms (replay seek). §4 gives the complete DDL for thirteen tables, all WAL-enabled, all with `DEDUP UPSERT KEYS`, partitioned by hour/day/month according to the query window and retention unit. §4.14 gives the operational settings. R0 exit criterion #6 requires "ticks, L2 deltas and 1-minute bars ... readable from QuestDB".

This ticket implements the tier behind the `MarketDataRepository` Protocol from E07-T01. It starts only after E07-K01 has confirmed (or replaced) QuestDB, so that no implementation effort is spent on a rejected engine; if the spike takes the ADR-0003 reversal path, this ticket is retargeted to TimescaleDB with the same Protocol, same tests and the same estimate - the Protocol is what makes that a retarget rather than a rewrite.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `backend/db/questdb/0001_core_tables.sql` and `0002_footprint_cells.sql` transcribing §4.1-§4.13 exactly: `trades`, `orderbook_deltas`, `orderbook_snapshots`, `tickers`, `klines`, `liquidations`, `open_interest`, `funding_rates`, `bars_time` (+ the other `bars_*` families), `footprint_cells`, `profiles`, `orderflow_metrics`, `heatmap_cells`, `engine_metrics`.
- Idempotent DDL runner keyed on a `_cv_migrations` table **inside QuestDB** (§9.1), run at boot by the storage service, never by request handlers.
- `storage/questdb/ilp_writer.py`: batched ILP-over-TCP writer, flush at **5 000 rows or 100 ms** per §4.14, per-table buffers, bounded queue with explicit backpressure (never silently drop - trades and executions must never be dropped, per `20-architecture.md` §3.1), reconnect with exponential backoff, and a `flush()` that is awaited on `stop()`.
- `storage/questdb/reader.py`: PGWire (8812) async pool using a **read-only** QuestDB user; parameterised queries only (no string interpolation of user input); per-shape query builders for §13.2 shapes 1-11.
- `storage/questdb/repository.py`: `MarketDataRepository` implementation passing the contract suite from E07-T01 unchanged.
- Engine settings applied and asserted at boot: `o3MaxLag=300s`, `maxUncommittedRows=500000`, explicit `SYMBOL CAPACITY` per §4 DDL, WAL on every table.
- Column-drift guard: at boot, the runner compares live table columns against the DDL files and raises `StorageSchemaDrift` rather than writing into a mismatched shape.
- Metrics + health wiring (see Observability).

## Out of scope
- Producing the derived values (`footprint_cells`, `profiles`, `orderflow_metrics`, `heatmap_cells` contents) - E18/E19/E21/E23. This ticket creates the tables and the write/read path only; a fixture-populated row proves the path.
- Export to Parquet and retention drops - E07-T04/T05.
- Ingestion from Bybit - E08 (this ticket is exercised from `packages/fixtures`).
- The `bars_*` builders themselves - E12.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given an empty QuestDB 8.x instance
When the storage service boots
Then all tables from 21-database-schema.md §4 exist with WAL enabled and the declared DEDUP UPSERT KEYS, and _cv_migrations records the applied DDL files

Given the DDL runner runs a second time against the same instance
When boot completes
Then no DDL is re-applied and boot adds under 200 ms, proving idempotency

Given one hour of recorded BTCUSDT trades from packages/fixtures
When they are written through MarketDataRepository.write_trades and then the same file is replayed a second time (simulating E08 resubscribe-on-gap)
Then the row count in `trades` is identical after both runs, proving DEDUP UPSERT KEYS idempotency end-to-end

Given trades for one symbol-day are present
When read_bars is called for bars_time/1m over that day
Then 100k bars return within 100 ms p95 on the reference profile, matching §13.2 shape #1

Given the replay seek shape
When read_book_snapshot_at(ts) then read_book_deltas(ts, ts+1min) are called
Then the snapshot seek completes within 200 ms and the applied deltas reproduce a book whose CRC32 matches orderbook_snapshots.checksum at the next snapshot anchor

Given QuestDB is stopped mid-write
When the ILP writer's queue fills
Then it applies backpressure and increments questdb_write_errors_total, no trade row is dropped, health() reports the tier degraded, and on reconnect the buffered batch is flushed exactly once

Given a table's live column set differs from the DDL file
When the service boots
Then it raises StorageSchemaDrift and refuses readiness instead of writing into a mismatched table

Given a symbol string containing a quote character
When it reaches a read query
Then the parameterised PGWire path escapes it and a SQL-injection test asserts no query-shape change
```

## Technical notes / design
Write path: one `asyncio.Queue` per table class; a single flusher task per table drains it, serialising rows into the ILP line format and writing to the socket. Timestamps are integer microseconds; the designated timestamp is always exchange event time and `recv_ts` is a plain column (§4 conventions). `SYMBOL` columns must be emitted as ILP *tags*, doubles as ILP fields - getting this wrong silently changes the storage shape, so a unit test asserts the serialised line for one golden row of each table.

Read path: asyncpg against PGWire. QuestDB has no secondary indexes; performance comes from the designated timestamp, partition granularity and `SYMBOL` equality filters (§13.2 closing note), so every query builder must (a) filter on `symbol` by equality, (b) bound `ts` on both sides, and (c) never `ORDER BY` a non-timestamp column. A lint test parses each builder's SQL and asserts these three properties.

`LATEST ON ts PARTITION BY symbol` is used for last price (shape #5); `SAMPLE BY` for roll-ups (#3, #8); `ASOF JOIN` for trade<->ticker alignment (#11).

Reversal path note: if E07-K01 selects TimescaleDB, `backend/db/questdb/*.sql` becomes an Alembic revision of hypertable DDL and `ilp_writer.py` becomes a `COPY`-based batch writer; the repository module name and the contract suite do not change.

## Test plan
- Unit: ILP line serialisation golden files per table; batch/flush trigger logic (5 000 rows vs 100 ms, whichever first) with a fake clock; backpressure behaviour at queue-full; query-builder lint (equality symbol filter, bounded ts, timestamp ordering); drift detector.
- Integration (testcontainers QuestDB): DDL idempotency; dedup replay; each of §13.2 shapes 1-11 returning correct results against a fixture dataset with a golden result file; book-reconstruction CRC check; connection-loss and reconnect.
- Contract: E07-T01 repository suite, run against the real engine.
- Perf: shapes A-F from E07-K01 re-run as a regression harness with the spike's `results.json` as the baseline; ILP sustained rows/s vs the >=600k target (§11.4).
- Chaos: covered by E07-Q04.
- Coverage target: >=85% on `storage/questdb/`.

## Security notes
- Read path uses a dedicated **read-only** QuestDB user; the service never issues DDL at runtime except the boot runner and the retention job (§4.14).
- QuestDB's HTTP console and its ports are not published to the host or tailnet (SR-048, threat S6 in `04-security-program.md` §5.8); the compose bind assertion from `E02-T08` covers this and this ticket adds a boot-time self-check enumerating listening sockets (SR-047).
- All queries parameterised; symbol/interval values are additionally validated against an allowlist derived from `instruments` before reaching SQL, because `SYMBOL` filters are the only user-controlled predicate.
- No credentials or PII in this tier (classification A-10, Internal); fixture data only in tests (SR: no real keys in fixtures, `03-testing-strategy.md` §11).

## Performance notes
Targets: §13.2 shapes #1-#11 as tabulated; ILP ingest >=600k rows/s sustained (§11.4, 20x headroom over the 25k rows/s peak for 5 symbols at 200 depth); write path must not contribute to the <=20 ms backend-internal fan-out budget (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §5.1 budget #6) - storage writes are off the fan-out path by construction (bus subscriber, not inline), and a test asserts the publisher does not await the writer.

title: Implement Parquet cold tier: hot->cold exporter with checksum manifest, compactor and DuckDB view layer
body:
## Context
Parquet is the archive, the replay source beyond the hot window, and - per ADR-0003 - "an open, portable archive format, an exit hatch even if every database choice changes". `21-database-schema.md` §5 specifies the Hive-partitioned directory layout (§5.1), the exact file-format rules (§5.2: Parquet v2, **ZSTD level 6**, 128 MiB row groups, 1 MiB pages, rows sorted by `ts` then `price`, dictionary on `symbol`/`side`/`action`/`tick_dir`, `TIMESTAMP(MICROS, UTC)`, SHA-256 per file in the manifest), the export job with its **non-negotiable ordering invariant** (§5.3), the compactor (§5.4) and the DuckDB view layer (§5.5). R0 exit criterion #6 requires "a DuckDB query returns one symbol-day".

The invariant, stated in §5.3, is the single most important line in this ticket: *no hot partition is ever dropped before its Parquet counterpart is written, checksummed and row-count-verified*; a crash between steps must leave duplicate data (harmless, dedup on read), never missing data.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `storage/cold/exporter.py` implementing the §5.3 flow: resolve retention policy -> select closed partitions older than `archive_after_days` -> read from QuestDB via PGWire into Arrow -> write Parquet per §5.2 -> SHA-256 + row-count verify against the source `COUNT` -> write manifest entry -> (hand the drop decision to E07-T05's reaper). On verify mismatch: write a `system_events` CRITICAL row, abort the run, keep the hot data.
- Directory layout exactly as §5.1 under `CV_COLD_ROOT` (`/var/lib/candleviewer/cold`, WSL `/mnt/data/candleviewer/cold`), including the `_manifests/` tree and `schema-registry.json`.
- Per-file provenance columns on every export: `_export_run_id STRING`, `_exported_at TIMESTAMP`, `_source STRING`.
- **Schema-drift fail-closed**: the exporter compares the column set against `cold/_manifests/schema-registry.json` and refuses to write on drift (§5.2 last paragraph).
- `storage/cold/manifest.py`: manifest read/write, per-file SHA-256, `verify_checksums()` used by the weekly scrub (SR-094) and on read.
- `storage/cold/compactor.py` per §5.4: trigger at >4 files per partition or any file <16 MiB with siblings; merge to one file per partition <=512 MiB; write `.tmp` -> fsync -> atomic rename -> delete originals, with row count and SHA-256 recorded **before** deletion; skip any partition referenced by an active `replay_sessions` row (idle guard).
- `storage/cold/duckdb_views.py`: builds `cold/analytics.duckdb` views from source on every start (they hold no state, §9.1), including `trades`, `orderbook_deltas`, `bars`, `footprint_cells`, `executions_cold`, `journal_all` and the analytics helpers `v_daily_pnl`, `v_session_tape_stats` from §5.5; `ATTACH ... AS pg (TYPE postgres, READ_ONLY)` using the `cv_ro` role from E07-T02.
- `ColdTierRepository` implementation satisfying the E07-T01 Protocol.
- **Dataset-id registry**: `query()` accepts a registered dataset id + partition predicates, never a filesystem path (SR-097).

## Out of scope
- Deciding *when* to export/drop and the retention policy engine - E07-T05 (this ticket exposes `export_partition` and `verify`, the reaper orchestrates).
- Cold-cold downsampling of `orderbook_deltas`/`heatmap_cells` past 180 days (§5.4 rollup rule) - deferred to **E16** with a TODO referencing this ticket; the `action='downsample'` branch raises `NotImplementedError` with that reference, and a test asserts the error rather than silent no-op.
- Backup/restic of the lake - E43/PRR (this ticket documents the path).
- Journal/OMS export producers (`oms/` subtree contents) - E41/E29; the layout and the writer support them, a fixture proves the shape.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given one closed symbol-day of trades in QuestDB
When the exporter runs for that partition
Then a Parquet file exists at cold/trades/symbol=BTCUSDT/dt=2026-11-10/part-0000.parquet, is Parquet v2 with ZSTD-6 compression and 128 MiB target row groups, is sorted by ts then price, and carries _export_run_id/_exported_at/_source

Given the exported file
When the manifest is read
Then it contains the file's SHA-256, row count and source table, and the row count equals the QuestDB COUNT(*) for that partition exactly

Given a deliberately corrupted byte in an exported Parquet file
When verify_checksums() runs (weekly scrub or on read)
Then the file is quarantined, a CRITICAL system_event and an alert are raised, and no reader is served data from it

Given the exporter is SIGKILLed after writing Parquet but before the manifest entry
When it is re-run
Then the partition is re-exported, the duplicate file is reconciled to a single manifest entry, and no rows are lost - and because the drop step is downstream, the hot partition is still present

Given the exporter detects a column present in QuestDB but absent from schema-registry.json
When it runs
Then it fails closed with StorageSchemaDrift, exports nothing and leaves the hot partition untouched

Given a partition directory with six 10 MiB files
When the compactor runs
Then it produces a single part-0000.parquet, records its row count and SHA-256 before deleting the originals, and the post-merge row count equals the sum of the inputs

Given a partition referenced by an active replay_sessions row
When the compactor runs
Then that partition is skipped and the skip is logged with the session id

Given cold/analytics.duckdb
When `SELECT count(*) FROM trades WHERE symbol='BTCUSDT' AND dt='2026-11-10'` is issued
Then it returns the exported row count within the §13.3 budget, satisfying R0 exit criterion 6

Given a query() call with dataset_id="../../etc/passwd" or a symlinked partition directory
When it is resolved
Then the registry rejects it, a path-traversal test asserts no filesystem read occurs outside CV_COLD_ROOT (SR-097)
```

## Technical notes / design
Read QuestDB partitions in `ts`-ordered chunks into `pyarrow.RecordBatch`es (target ~1 M rows for trades, ~4 M for deltas so a row group lands near 128 MiB), then `pyarrow.parquet.ParquetWriter(..., version="2.6", compression="zstd", compression_level=6, data_page_size=1<<20, write_statistics=["ts","price","notional","symbol"], use_dictionary=["symbol","side","action","tick_dir"])`. Sorting matters twice - for min/max pruning and for the cheap merge on read - so the writer asserts monotonic `ts` per row group and fails otherwise rather than writing an unsorted file that silently defeats §13.3.

Timestamps must be written as `TIMESTAMP(isAdjustedToUTC=true, unit=MICROS)` to match QuestDB microsecond resolution exactly; a round-trip test asserts no precision loss. Market data stays `DOUBLE`; OMS exports use `DECIMAL(38,18)` (§5.2) - two different writer profiles, selected by dataset id, not by guessing.

Atomicity: every write goes to `part-NNNN.parquet.tmp`, is fsynced, then `os.rename`d within the same directory (rename is atomic on the same filesystem); the manifest entry is appended after the rename. Crash ordering is therefore: file present without manifest (recoverable, re-export) is possible; manifest without file is not.

DuckDB views are recreated from source at every start; the `postgres` extension attachment is `READ_ONLY` with `cv_ro`, which is what prevents an analytics query from ever mutating the ledger.

## Test plan
- Unit: writer profile selection; row-group sizing maths; sort assertion; provenance columns; manifest SHA-256 and append semantics; drift detector; compaction trigger rules and idle guard; dataset-id registry rejection cases (traversal, symlink, absolute path, unregistered id).
- Integration (testcontainers QuestDB + a tmpfs cold root): full export of a fixture symbol-day with row-count parity; corrupted-file scrub; kill-and-resume at each of the three crash points (after write, after checksum, after manifest); compaction of a many-small-files partition; DuckDB symbol-day query returning the exact count; `journal_all` union view across Parquet + Postgres.
- Contract: `ColdTierRepository` suite from E07-T01.
- Perf: export throughput vs the >=200 MB/s write target (§11.4); DuckDB cold-replay scan vs <500 ms/hour of deltas and <2 s/month for trades (§13.3); compression ratio recorded against the 0.5-0.75 GB/day/symbol planning figure (budget #12) and reported so E16 can replace the estimate.
- Coverage target: >=85% on `storage/cold/`.

## Security notes
Threats from `04-security-program.md` §5.8: **S1** silent Parquet corruption -> SR-094 per-file checksum manifest verified on read and by the weekly scrub, with quarantine + alert; **S3** path traversal via export/replay endpoints -> SR-097 registry-addressed datasets, zero user-supplied paths, mandatory traversal and symlink-escape tests (both present in the AC); **S6** DuckDB console exposure -> the DuckDB file is opened in-process only, no server mode, no published port (SR-048). Backups of the lake are encrypted with a key distinct from the runtime KEK (SR-091/SR-092) - documented here, automated in E43. Data classification A-10/A-13. This ticket carries the `security` label and requires Security engineer review before merge.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no UI.

## Performance notes
Budgets: Parquet export >=200 MB/s (§11.4); DuckDB replay scan >=1 GB/s from page cache (§11.4) and the §13.3 per-caller targets; storage growth budget #12 with 0.75 GB/day/symbol as the provisioning figure. The compactor exists specifically because unsorted small files defeat both row-group pruning and the sort-order merge (§13.3 closing note) - its effect is measured before/after and recorded.

## Observability
`storage_export_rows_total{stream,result}`, `storage_export_bytes_total{stream}`, `storage_export_duration_seconds{stream}`, `storage_export_verify_failures_total`, `storage_compaction_files_merged_total`, `storage_cold_bytes{stream}`, `storage_scrub_mismatches_total`. `system_events` CRITICAL on verify failure and on quarantine; audit entry for compaction-triggered deletions. These feed the SCR-142 panel designed in E07-D01.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All AC green, including all three crash-point resume tests.
- [ ] Coverage >=85% on `storage/cold/`.
- [ ] Measured compression ratio and export throughput recorded in the PR and in `21-database-schema.md` §14 open-to-verify items.
- [ ] Security engineer sign-off on SR-094/SR-097 controls.
- [ ] QA sign-off (E07-Q01 cases).

- `E07-T02` - the `cv_ro` role for the DuckDB Postgres attachment and the `replay_sessions`/`backups` tables' existence for the idle guard and run records (tables land with their owning revisions; until then the guard reads an empty set and a test covers that path).
- Consumed by `E07-T05` (reaper) and by E16/E26.

title: Build retention/archive job skeleton and the source_tier=auto query router
body:
## Context
Two mechanisms turn three separate stores into one coherent data tier, and both are E07's responsibility:

1. **The retention/archive job** - `21-database-schema.md` §6 (lifecycle Live -> Hot -> Archive -> Downsample -> Purge, pinning, disk-pressure behaviour) and §7 (the per-stream retention matrix, e.g. `orderbook_deltas` 7 d hot / 180 d raw cold, `trades` 30 d hot / 24 mo cold, pinned = infinite everywhere). `24-internal-schemas.md` specifies the daily job at 03:00 UTC that "never touches pinned data; never deletes a period referenced by an unexported journal trade, a saved replay session or an open investigation", with an emergency pass under disk pressure that "raises a critical alert **before** deleting anything".
2. **The tier router** - `21-database-schema.md` §5.5: "if `range_start >= now() - hot_retention(stream)` -> QuestDB; if fully older -> DuckDB; if straddling -> both, merged by `ts` with dedup on the natural key. The merge is implemented once in `backend/storage/router.py` and contract-tested with an overlap fixture."

This is a **skeleton** in R0 scope: the engine, the safety invariants and the router are real and tested; the operator surface (recorded-symbol management, per-symbol caps, the admin screen) belongs to E16/E42. The threat model E07-X01 must be Done first, because SR-096/SR-099 shape this job's control flow.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `storage/retention/policy.py` - loads `retention_policies` (Postgres, §3.6.3) with the §7 defaults seeded from `backend/db/seeds/retention_defaults.yaml`; most-specific-first evaluation (per-symbol beats global), matching the `/recording/retention-policies` semantics in `22-api-openapi.yaml`.
- `storage/retention/reaper.py` - the daily job: **dry-run first, always**, producing a report (symbol, stream, range, row count, bytes) before any destructive action; `apply()` executes only what the report listed; every deletion writes an audit entry (SR-099).
- Blocking predicates, each individually tested: pinned symbol (`recorded_symbols.pinned AND removed_at IS NULL`); partition referenced by an active `replay_sessions` row; partition not yet exported+verified to cold (the §5.3 ordering invariant); unexported journal trade in range.
- Disk-pressure behaviour per §6 and SR-096: below 15 % free -> accelerated mode (non-pinned symbols in ascending `recorded_symbols.priority`, effective retention halved, `warning` system event per affected symbol) until free > 25 %; below 5 % free -> ingestion paused for non-pinned auto-recorded symbols with a `critical` event. Alert is raised **before** any deletion.
- Orchestration of E07-T04's exporter: export -> verify -> only then `ALTER TABLE ... DROP PARTITION` (QuestDB) / partition-directory delete (cold).
- `storage/router.py` - `source_tier` resolution (`hot | cold | auto`) with the straddle merge: merge by `ts`, dedup on the stream's natural key (the same key as the QuestDB `DEDUP UPSERT KEYS` clause), and every response states which tier(s) served it (the `22-api-openapi.yaml` read endpoints declare this - "Each response states which" tier served the window).
- Scheduler registration (03:00 UTC retention, 02:15 UTC export per §5.3, 03:00 Sunday compaction per §5.4) behind a feature flag so it is off by default in dev.

## Out of scope
- Recorded-symbol CRUD, auto-record triggers, per-symbol caps and priorities as a *user-managed* surface - **E16** (M11). This ticket reads `recorded_symbols` and honours it; it does not manage it.
- `GET /api/v1/recording/storage` and `/recording/retention-policies` HTTP endpoints - E16/E42; this ticket produces the `StorageUsage` data shape internally and a unit test asserts it matches the OpenAPI schema.
- Cold-cold downsampling (`action='downsample'`) - E16, per E07-T04's out-of-scope note.
- The SCR-140/SCR-142 screens - E42.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given default retention policies and a symbol with 40 days of trades in QuestDB
When the reaper runs in dry-run mode
Then it reports exactly the partitions older than 30 days, with row counts and byte estimates, and deletes nothing

Given the same state and a pinned symbol
When apply() runs
Then no partition of the pinned symbol is dropped at either tier, and the skip reason "pinned" appears in the report

Given a partition that has not yet been exported and verified to Parquet
When apply() runs
Then the drop is refused with STORAGE_RETENTION_BLOCKED_* and the run continues with the remaining partitions rather than aborting wholesale

Given an active replay_sessions row referencing a cold partition
When apply() runs
Then that partition directory is not deleted and the skip is logged with the session id

Given every deletion performed by a run
When the audit log is inspected
Then there is one append-only entry per deletion carrying symbol, stream, time range and freed bytes (SR-099)

Given free disk falls below 15 percent
When the reaper runs
Then it enters accelerated mode, processes non-pinned symbols in ascending priority with halved effective retention, and raises a warning system event per affected symbol BEFORE deleting anything

Given free disk falls below 5 percent
When the guard evaluates
Then recording for non-pinned auto-recorded symbols is paused, a critical event is raised, and the trading path remains functional because it does not share the recording volume (SR-096)

Given a read whose range lies entirely inside the hot window
When the router resolves it
Then it queries QuestDB only, and the response reports tier="hot"

Given a read whose range straddles the hot/cold boundary
When the router resolves it
Then both tiers are queried, results are merged by ts and deduplicated on the natural key with zero duplicate rows at the seam and zero gaps, verified by the overlap fixture, and the response reports tier="both"

Given a read whose range is entirely older than the hot window
When the router resolves it
Then DuckDB serves it and the response reports tier="cold"
```

## Technical notes / design
Reaper control flow, in order (the order is a safety property, not a style choice):
```
plan = policy.resolve(all_streams)            # most-specific-first
plan = plan.exclude(pinned)                   # SR-099
plan = plan.exclude(referenced_by_replay)
plan = plan.exclude(not_exported_or_unverified)   # §5.3 invariant
report = plan.dry_run()                       # persisted, audited
if disk.free_pct < 15: report = report.accelerate()   # alert FIRST
audit.write(report)
for item in report: storage.drop(item); audit.write(deletion(item))
```
Every step is idempotent and resumable - a run killed halfway leaves a consistent state and the next run re-derives the plan from current facts rather than from a cached plan.

Router straddle merge:
```python
async def read(stream, sym, rng, tier="auto"):
    boundary = now_us() - hot_retention_us(stream)
    if tier == "hot" or rng.start >= boundary:   return await hot.read(...)
    if tier == "cold" or rng.end < boundary:     return await cold.read(...)
    hot_rows, cold_rows = await gather(hot.read(...), cold.read(...))
    return dedup_merge(cold_rows, hot_rows, key=NATURAL_KEY[stream])  # hot wins ties
```
Hot wins ties because the hot row is the freshest representation after a dedup upsert. `NATURAL_KEY` is derived from the same constant that generates the QuestDB `DEDUP UPSERT KEYS` clause in E07-T03 - one definition, two consumers, asserted equal by a test, so the two can never drift.

Config keys: `CV_RECORDER_HOT_DAYS` (7), `CV_RECORDER_RETENTION_DAYS` (30), `CV_STORAGE_MIN_FREE_PCT` (15), `CV_STORAGE_CRITICAL_FREE_PCT` (5), `CV_RETENTION_CRON` (`0 3 * * *`), `CV_EXPORT_CRON` (`15 2 * * *`), `CV_COMPACT_CRON` (`0 3 * * 0`), `CV_RETENTION_ENABLED` (false in dev).

Error codes: `STORAGE_RETENTION_BLOCKED_BY_PIN`, `STORAGE_RETENTION_BLOCKED_UNVERIFIED`, `STORAGE_RETENTION_BLOCKED_REPLAY`, `STORAGE_DISK_CRITICAL`.

## Test plan
- Unit: policy resolution precedence (global vs per-symbol vs pinned); each blocking predicate in isolation and in combination; accelerated-mode ordering by priority; alert-before-delete ordering (a test asserts the event is emitted before any drop call, using a call-order spy); router boundary maths at exactly `now - hot_retention` (inclusive/exclusive off-by-one is the classic bug here - explicit cases at boundary-1us, boundary, boundary+1us).
- Contract: the §5.5 overlap fixture - a dataset deliberately present in *both* tiers for a 10-minute window, asserting the merged output has the same row count as the union-by-natural-key and is `ts`-ordered.
- Integration: full export -> verify -> drop cycle against QuestDB + cold root; dry-run report matches what apply() actually deletes, row for row; pinned symbol survives a full cycle; audit entries present and hash-chain-valid.
- Chaos: E07-Q04 covers kill-mid-drop and disk-full.
- Coverage target: >=85% on `storage/retention/` and `storage/router.py`.

## Security notes
Directly implements threats S2 (disk exhaustion takes trading down - **Critical**) and S5 (retention deletes pinned data) from `04-security-program.md` §5.8, via SR-096 (separate volume, 75 %/90 % thresholds, recorder pauses before trading is affected) and SR-099 (pins honoured, dry-run first, every deletion audited). Retention *policy changes* are a dangerous action requiring the `retention.change` permission with a before/after audit entry (`21-database-schema.md` §7 closing note) - this ticket enforces the permission check at the service boundary even though the screen that calls it is E42's. The reaper runs as a scheduled internal job with no user-supplied paths (SR-097). Requires E07-X01 threat model Done before merge.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no UI. The data shape it produces is what SCR-142 renders (E07-D01); units and per-tier separation in the payload are what let that screen state figures as text.

## Performance notes
Retention reaper: QuestDB `DROP PARTITION` is partition-metadata-only, target <1 s (§13.2 shape #12). The whole nightly export window must complete inside the off-peak window - §11.4 gives >=200 MB/s export, so 13 GB/symbol completes in minutes. The reaper must not contend with ingestion: it runs at 03:00 UTC and yields between partitions, with a test asserting event-loop lag stays within the 50-100 ms threshold (`03-testing-strategy.md` §6) during a run.

## Observability

Audit: one entry per deletion and per policy change. Grafana panel additions handed to E04.

title: Define the operator content model for storage telemetry and review the StorageUsage contract
body:
## Context
**Correction of scope (DoR gate finding #2).** This ticket previously drew the SCR-142 hi-fi. That was wrong: E07 is a
backend-platform infrastructure epic with **no FE/UI Story children**, so a screen design parked here had no consuming
engineering deliverable inside the epic, and it duplicated **E16-D04** (`Design SCR-142 storage & database panel with tier
health and projections`, Sprint 05), which is the real owner of that screen alongside **E16-S04** (implementation,
Sprint 08) and **E16-D07** (design QA, Sprint 09). Screen design, states, redlines and Figma for SCR-142 now live wholly in
E16.

What E07 *does* own, and what this ticket now delivers, is the thing E16 cannot design without: the **operator content
model** - the decision list, the vocabulary, the units and the severity semantics that the storage tier must expose - and
the review of `GET /api/v1/recording/storage` / schema `StorageUsage` against it. That contract is a concrete E07
engineering deliverable (authored by **E07-T05**, fed by E07-T03/T04 metrics), so this ticket validates an artefact that
actually ships inside E07, in the same train, and hands E16-D04 a settled input three sprints before it starts.

Plan material: `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` (`GET /recording/storage`, schema `StorageUsage`),
`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §6 (lifecycle), §7 (retention matrix), §11 (sizing/growth),
`docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-142 (downstream consumer, for traceability only),
`docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-REC-004, US-REC-005, US-REC-007, `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §12 (storage metrics).

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Operator decision list** (the core artefact): a one-page, Owner-validated statement of the decisions storage telemetry
  must support - "am I about to run out of disk", "what stops working first", "is a migration pending", "is a tier lagging
  or unreachable", "is this symbol's data pinned". One row per decision: the question, the field(s) that answer it, the
  threshold that makes it urgent, the action available.
- **Field-by-field contract review of `StorageUsage`** against that list: `tiers[]` (questdb / parquet / postgres with
  `used_bytes`, `retention_days`), `symbols[]` (`used_bytes`, `daily_growth_bytes`, `pinned`), `disk_total_bytes`,
  `disk_free_bytes`, `daily_growth_bytes`, `projected_full_at`, `generated_at`. Every decision must be answerable from a
  real field; every field must answer something. Gaps are filed as contract changes against **E07-T05** *before* T05
  merges - that is the whole point of scheduling this in Sprint 02.
- **Severity + degradation vocabulary**: the canonical wording for the states the tier can enter - healthy, migration
  pending (version delta), lag warning, accelerated retention (<15 % free), critical / read-only (<5 % free, recording
  paused), `STORAGE_TIER_UNAVAILABLE`, `STORAGE_EXPORT_VERIFY_FAILED` (hot data deliberately retained - **safe**, not
  broken), `STORAGE_SCHEMA_DRIFT`. Each gets a text label, a plain-language consequence sentence, and the ordering rule
  "recording pauses before trading is affected".
- **Units & formatting rules**: byte magnitudes, growth per day, projection formatting and the uncertainty caveat on
  `projected_full_at` (§11 flags the underlying growth figure as an estimate until real recording data lands), plus the
  `generated_at` / 60 s sampling semantics (sampled, not streamed).
- **Audited-action semantics**: `storage.compaction_triggered`, `storage.vacuum_triggered`,
  `storage.tier_migration_triggered` - each specified as requiring a confirm step and an owner-level RBAC scope
  (`x-rbac` in `22-api-openapi.yaml`), so E07-T05's endpoint and E16's future UI agree.
- **Handoff note to E16-D04**: all of the above as markdown committed under `docs/plan/` handoff material, explicitly named
  as the input for E16-D04 and E16-S04.

## Out of scope
- **The SCR-142 screen itself** - wireframes, hi-fi, layout, component mapping, motion, redlines, Figma: **E16-D04**.
- SCR-140 recorder screen, SCR-141 retention editor: **E16-D02/D03**.
- SCR-143 system health: E04.
- Any React implementation: **E16-S04**.
- New design-system components (propose to E05; none are expected, since this ticket ships no visual design).
- a11y audit of a rendered screen: **E16-Q05** (this ticket only fixes the text-not-colour rule at the vocabulary level).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given the operator decision list reviewed with the Owner
When each decision row is checked against the StorageUsage schema in 22-api-openapi.yaml
Then every decision is answerable from at least one real field, and every field maps to at least one decision, or the
  exception is recorded as an accepted decision with a one-line reason

Given a decision that no current field answers
When the review completes
Then a contract-change item is filed against E07-T05 with the proposed field, type and unit, and E07-T05 cannot merge
  until each such item is either implemented or explicitly rejected by the Architect

Given the severity vocabulary
When STORAGE_EXPORT_VERIFY_FAILED is described
Then the consequence sentence states that hot data was deliberately retained and no data was lost, so the state reads as
  attention-needed rather than as a generic failure

Given the degradation ordering rule
When an operator reads the critical-state copy
Then the sentence states in text - not by colour, icon or position alone - that recording pauses before trading is
  affected, and that pinned symbols are exempt from accelerated retention

Given the handoff note
When the E16-D04 designer reads it cold in Sprint 05
Then they can draw SCR-142 without reopening the contract, verified by a walkthrough recorded on this ticket
```

## Technical notes / design
Work from the payload E07-T05's integration test actually emits, not the OpenAPI `example` block - the divergence between
the two is where this class of defect lives. Where a decision needs a field that does not exist, prefer extending
`StorageUsage` over having the UI compute it, so that E16's screen and any future CLI/alert consumer share one source of
truth. `projected_full_at` is a projection from `daily_growth_bytes`; specify it as nullable with an explicit
"insufficient history" sentinel rather than a misleading far-future date. Sparkline series, if added, are capped at a fixed
sample count so the payload stays bounded.

- **Reachable-state coverage audit**: drive the storage tier into each state the implementation can actually reach and

Given a tier is stopped so the API cannot reach QuestDB
When GET /api/v1/recording/storage is called
Then the response reports STORAGE_TIER_UNAVAILABLE for that tier, still returns valid data for the reachable tiers, and
  distinguishes "unreachable" from "reachable but empty"

Given an export whose checksum verification failed
When the payload is inspected
Then STORAGE_EXPORT_VERIFY_FAILED is reported together with a field or text indicating hot data was retained and no data

Given free disk is forced below 5 percent
When the payload is inspected
Then the critical state is expressed as a machine-readable enum plus a human text consequence stating that recording

Given daily_growth_bytes has insufficient history to project
When projected_full_at is read

When every string field and error message is scanned

Reconciliation runs against captured real responses, never the OpenAPI `example`. Drive the degraded states with the same
