title: QA: black-box test plan and storage contract/integration suite for the three tiers
body:
## Context
`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.1 requires every Story to ship with a QA-authored or QA-reviewed test plan before development starts, and `03-testing-strategy.md` §"test plans" requires it to live inline in the backlog ticket so it travels with the work. E07 has no user-facing story surface, so its QA artifact is a **black-box plan against the storage tier's observable behaviour**: what goes in through the repository API comes out unchanged, at the right tier, with the right dedup, and nothing is ever lost.

`03-testing-strategy.md` §5 defines the integration environment this suite runs in (`docker-compose.test.yml` with QuestDB + Postgres + a fixture-replay mock, `testcontainers-python` for finer-grained suites, **no network egress**) and §5 names the exact scenario this epic must cover end to end: "Recorder: auto-record trigger -> QuestDB write -> retention/pin logic -> Parquet roll-off to cold tier -> DuckDB query of rolled-off data."

## Scope / Deliverables
- The black-box test plan document (`docs/qa/plans/E07-storage.md`), organised by observable behaviour, not by implementation file: write-read fidelity, idempotency, tier routing, lifecycle, safety invariants, failure surfaces.
- The shared **repository contract suite** parametrised over implementations - authored jointly with E07-T01, executed here against real engines: every `MarketDataRepository`, `ColdTierRepository` and UoW method, with the same assertions for the fake and the real implementation.
- Integration suite additions to `docker-compose.test.yml` runs:
  - Fixture replay -> QuestDB -> read back: row counts, value fidelity (no float drift), `ts` ordering, microsecond precision preserved end to end.
  - Dedup/idempotency: replay the same fixture twice and three times; assert stable row counts for every table with a `DEDUP UPSERT KEYS` clause.
  - Out-of-order delivery within `o3MaxLag`: shuffled fixture still yields a `ts`-ordered read.
  - Full lifecycle: write -> export -> verify -> drop -> DuckDB read returns the same rows (the §5 scenario).
  - Tier routing: hot-only, cold-only and straddling ranges, using the overlap fixture; assert zero duplicates and zero gaps at the seam.
  - Postgres: migration up/down/up, role privilege matrix, UoW transaction boundaries and savepoints.
- Negative/edge cases: empty range; range entirely in the future; symbol with no data; a single-row partition; a partition spanning a DST-irrelevant but month-boundary edge; `ts` exactly at the hot/cold boundary (boundary-1us / boundary / boundary+1us).
- Golden-file fixtures for each §13.2 query shape's result set, regenerable only via `--update-golden` with a written rationale (`03-testing-strategy.md` §4.2).
- CI wiring: the suite runs in the `integration` gate; flaky-test quarantine policy applied.

## Out of scope
- Perf/load measurement - E07-Q03.
- Chaos/failure injection - E07-Q04.
- Security control verification - E07-X02.
- UI testing - no UI in this epic (SCR-142 is designed here, built in E42).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given the black-box plan
When a reviewer cross-references it against E07's tickets
Then every acceptance-criteria scenario in E07-T02, E07-T03, E07-T04 and E07-T05 maps to at least one plan case, and the plan additionally contains cases no ticket listed (negative and edge coverage)

Given the contract suite
When it is run against the fakes and against QuestDB+Postgres+cold
Then it passes unchanged in all cases, proving the abstraction that ADR-0003 depends on

Given one symbol-day fixture replayed through the full lifecycle
When export, verify, drop and a DuckDB read are executed in sequence
Then the DuckDB row count and a checksum over the sorted rows equal the pre-export QuestDB values exactly

Given the overlap fixture spanning the hot/cold boundary
When the router serves a straddling range
Then the merged result has no duplicate natural keys and no missing rows compared to the union of both tiers

Given the same fixture replayed three times
When row counts are compared
Then they are identical after each replay for every dedup-keyed table

Given a test in this suite fails intermittently twice in a week
When the flake policy is applied
Then it is quarantined the same day with a tracking ticket, per 03-testing-strategy.md

Given the suite runs in CI
When the integration gate executes
Then it completes without network egress and within the gate's time budget
```

## Technical notes / design
The suite is parametrised at the fixture level: one `pytest` fixture yields an implementation tuple (`fake`, `real`), and the same test bodies run for both - this is the mechanism that proves the ADR-0003 abstraction rather than asserting it. Heavy cases are marked `@pytest.mark.slow` and excluded from the per-PR gate.

Value-fidelity assertions compare floats with an explicit tolerance of 0 for prices/sizes (they must round-trip exactly through `DOUBLE`) and 1e-9 for derived aggregates; microsecond timestamps are compared as integers, never as datetimes, because a datetime comparison hides a µs truncation bug.

Golden result files are stored per query shape under `packages/fixtures/golden/storage/`; regeneration requires `--update-golden` plus a written rationale in the PR description (`03-testing-strategy.md` §4.2).

## Test plan
(This ticket *is* a test plan; this section records how the plan itself is validated.)
- Peer review by the second QA/SDET and by the backend lead.
- Traceability matrix row per E07 ticket AC -> plan case id, committed alongside the plan.
- A deliberate mutation exercise: introduce three seeded defects (drop the dedup clause on one table; off-by-one on the router boundary; skip the row-count verify in export) and confirm the suite catches all three. Any miss is a coverage gap fixed before sign-off.
- Coverage contribution recorded toward the >=85% backend threshold.

## Security notes
Fixtures only; no real Bybit keys or account identifiers, enforced by the CI lint that scans fixture files for real-key-shaped patterns (`03-testing-strategy.md` §11). The integration environment has no network egress. Test databases start empty every run - no shared mutable state across CI runs.

## Performance notes
The suite must stay inside the `integration` gate budget; heavy volume cases (100k bars, full symbol-day) are marked `slow` and run in the nightly job rather than per-PR, per `03-testing-strategy.md`.

## Observability

title: QA: exploratory charter - tier boundaries, backfill idempotency and lifecycle surprises
body:
## Context
Scripted suites find the defects someone anticipated. The storage tier's dangerous defects are the ones nobody wrote a case for: a partition that is exported twice and counted once, a pin applied *during* a reaper run, a symbol renamed on the exchange, a clock that steps backwards across the export window. `03-testing-strategy.md` mandates exploratory charters alongside scripted coverage; this is E07's.

## Scope / Deliverables
Four timeboxed session-based charters (90 minutes each, session notes committed to `docs/qa/exploratory/E07-*.md`):

1. **Charter: tier boundary.** "Explore reads whose ranges interact with the hot/cold boundary, with the boundary moving underneath them, to discover gaps, duplicates or ordering breaks." Includes: a read issued while the reaper drops the partition it is reading; a range whose boundary crosses during a long scan; `hot_retention` changed mid-flight; clock stepping backwards.
2. **Charter: backfill and replay idempotency.** "Explore repeated and partial ingestion of the same data to discover row-count drift." Includes: replay a fixture with one field altered (does dedup treat it as the same row or a new one - and is that the intended semantic per the `DEDUP UPSERT KEYS` of that table?); interleave two symbols' replays; replay an overlapping window with different `epoch_id`; ingest a row whose `ts` is older than the current partition retention horizon.
3. **Charter: retention safety.** "Explore ways to make the reaper delete something it must not." Includes: pin applied mid-run; pin removed mid-run; `replay_sessions` row created between dry-run and apply; a journal trade referencing a range about to be purged; two reaper instances racing; accelerated mode entered while a manual compaction is in progress.
4. **Charter: operator's mental model.** "Read the storage state the way an operator would from the E07-D01 design and the real payload, and find where the system's truth and the screen's story diverge." Includes: `projected_full_at` after a growth spike; per-symbol figures during an export; what the panel shows while a tier is unreachable.

Deliverables per session: charter, duration, areas covered, bugs found with severity, questions raised, and follow-up test cases to promote into the scripted suite (E07-Q01).

## Out of scope
- Deliberate infrastructure failure injection (kill containers, fill disks) - E07-Q04 owns that as scripted chaos.
- Performance measurement - E07-Q03.
- Fixing the defects found (filed as Bugs against the owning ticket).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given four charters
When each session is run
Then session notes are committed with duration, coverage, findings and follow-ups, per the session-based test management format

Given any defect found
When it is filed
Then it has reproduction steps, environment, expected vs actual and a severity, satisfying the Bug DoR in 02-definition-of-ready-done.md §6.1

Given a finding that reveals a missing scripted case
When the session closes
Then the case is promoted into E07-Q01's suite in the same sprint, not left in the notes

Given charter 3 discovers any path that deletes pinned data
When it is triaged
Then it is priority/p0 regardless of likelihood, because pinned data loss is unrecoverable (no REST tick history)

Given all four sessions complete with zero P0/P1 findings outstanding
When QA reviews
Then the epic-level exploratory pass required by the Epic DoD is recorded as done
```

## Technical notes / design
Session-based test management: each charter is a timeboxed mission, not a script. Notes follow the standard sections (charter, duration, areas, findings, questions, follow-ups) and are committed so the reasoning survives the session.

Each session runs on its own scratch compose stack seeded from fixtures, so one charter's residue cannot explain another's finding. The tester works from the operator's surfaces only - logs, metrics, `system_events`, audit entries, and the E07-D01 payload - because a finding that required reading the source would not have been findable in production.

## Test plan
Session-based test management: each charter is timeboxed, notes follow the standard sections, and the debrief with the backend lead happens within one working day so findings are actionable while context is fresh. Fixtures from `packages/fixtures`; a scratch compose stack per session so state is never shared between charters.

## Security notes
Charter 3 overlaps the SR-099 control surface (pins honoured, dry-run first, deletions audited) - any finding there is copied to E07-X02 and to the Security engineer, since it is a control failure, not merely a bug. No real credentials are used in any session.

## Accessibility notes
Charter 4 reviews the operator narrative but not an implemented UI; a11y findings, if any, are routed to E07-D02.

## Performance notes
Observations only (e.g. "the reaper made reads slow for 40 s") are recorded and handed to E07-Q03 for measurement rather than judged here.

## Observability
Sessions deliberately use only what an operator would have - logs, metrics, `system_events`, audit entries. Where a session could not answer a question from those sources, that gap is itself a finding filed against E07's observability deliverables.

title: QA: storage performance harness - ILP ingest rate, query-shape regression, export throughput
body:
## Context
E07-K01 measured two engines once, to make a decision. This ticket turns that one-off measurement into a **repeatable harness with recorded baselines**, so the numbers ADR-0008 is built on cannot silently rot as the code changes. `30-release-roadmap.md` §4.4 sets the R0 perf gate as "benchmark harness committed and runnable in CI (numbers recorded, not yet gating)" - recorded now, gating from R5/E46.

Budgets come from `21-database-schema.md` §11.4 (throughput) and §13.2/§13.3 (per-shape latency), plus `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §2 budget #12 (storage growth) and §6 (ingestion, memory, storage).

## Scope / Deliverables
- `tests/perf/storage/` harness, runnable locally and in the nightly CI job, reusing the E07-K01 shape definitions so the numbers are directly comparable to ADR-0008's table.
- **Ingest**: sustained ILP rows/s via the real `ilp_writer`, for 10 minutes at the 5-symbol/200-depth profile (~25k rows/s realistic) and at a stress profile pushed until the queue backs up; reports achieved rows/s, p95 `questdb_write_seconds`, queue depth, and the backpressure onset point against the >=600k rows/s headroom claim.
- **Query shapes**: shapes #1-#11 from §13.2 run warm and cold-cache, 30 samples each, p50/p95/p99, compared against a committed `baseline.json`; a >20 % p95 regression fails the nightly job and opens a ticket (it does not block PRs in R0).
- **Cold tier**: Parquet export throughput MB/s vs the >=200 MB/s target; DuckDB scans vs §13.3 targets (cold replay <500 ms/hour of deltas, journal analytics <1 s over 12 months, trades <2 s/month, big-print research <1 s/month, audit export <500 ms/month); compaction before/after effect on scan time (this is the measurement that justifies the compactor's existence).
- **Storage growth**: measured compressed bytes/day/symbol at 200 depth from a real (or fixture-replayed) 24 h run, reported against the 0.5-0.75 GB/day planning range of budget #12 - this is the number `21-database-schema.md` §11 and `24-internal-schemas.md` explicitly flag as an estimate awaiting measurement.
- **Reaper impact**: event-loop lag during a retention run, against the 50-100 ms threshold of `03-testing-strategy.md` §6.
- Results published as a markdown table plus `results.json` per run; the R0 numbers appended to ADR-0008 and to `21-database-schema.md` §14.

## Out of scope
- API/WS load testing (k6/Locust) - E04/E46.
- Chart-engine FPS - E06.
- Making these gates blocking - E46 (R5).
- Multi-node scaling.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given the harness and a seeded dataset
When it runs on the reference VPS profile (4 vCPU / 8 GB container limits)
Then it produces p50/p95/p99 for shapes #1-#11, ingest rows/s, export MB/s, DuckDB scan times and measured bytes/day/symbol, all in one results.json

Given a committed baseline.json
When a run's p95 for any shape exceeds the baseline by more than 20 percent
Then the nightly job fails with a report naming the shape and the delta, and does not fail per-PR builds in R0

Given the ILP stress profile
When the writer is pushed past its drain rate
Then the harness records the backpressure onset rows/s and confirms zero trade rows were dropped, matching the never-drop-trades invariant

Given a partition with many small files, measured before and after compaction
When DuckDB scan time is compared
Then the improvement is quantified and recorded, justifying the compactor per 21-database-schema.md §13.3

Given a 24 h recording (or equivalent fixture replay)
When storage growth is measured
Then a real bytes/day/symbol figure is recorded and 21-database-schema.md §11 and §14 are updated, replacing the estimate

Given the retention reaper runs during the measurement window
When event-loop lag is sampled
Then it stays within the 50-100 ms threshold, or the excess is filed as a perf defect against E07-T05
```

## Technical notes / design
Shape definitions are imported from the E07-K01 harness module rather than re-typed, so ADR-0008's numbers and this harness's numbers remain directly comparable; a test asserts the shape-id set is identical to the ADR's table.

Warm and cold runs are recorded as separate series and never averaged together. Cold runs drop the page cache between iterations (container restart in CI); warm runs execute 5 discarded iterations before sampling. Every result row carries its conditions (`engine`, `cache`, `cpu_limit`, `mem_limit`, `dataset_id`, `commit_sha`) so a number can never be quoted without them.

Percentiles are computed with the nearest-rank method over >=30 samples; runs with fewer samples are reported as raw values, not percentiles, to avoid manufacturing precision.

## Test plan
The harness has its own unit tests (timer correctness on a synthetic workload of known duration; percentile maths against a known distribution; baseline-comparison logic including the boundary at exactly 20 %). Cold-cache runs drop the page cache between iterations and are labelled separately from warm runs - conflating the two is the most common way a storage benchmark lies. Every number reports its measurement conditions inline.

## Security notes
Runs against fixtures in an egress-free environment. Stress profiles must not be pointed at any shared or production-like instance - the harness refuses to run unless `CV_ENV=test` (an assertion, not a convention). Results contain no credentials or real account identifiers.

## Accessibility notes
N/A.

## Performance notes
This ticket *is* the performance verification for E07. Targets: §11.4 (ILP >=600k rows/s, Parquet export >=200 MB/s, DuckDB >=1 GB/s page-cache scan, PG <=50 tx/s), §13.2/§13.3 per-shape, budget #12 storage growth, §6 memory ceiling (<=300 MB/symbol backend) sampled during the ingest run.

## Observability
Harness scrapes the storage metrics rather than instrumenting separately, which doubles as a test that those metrics are accurate: a metric that disagrees with the harness's own timer is a defect.

title: QA: chaos scenarios - DB down, disk full, crash between export and partition drop
body:
## Context
`03-testing-strategy.md` §"chaos" names the storage failure explicitly: **"DB down (QuestDB or Postgres unavailable)"** - docker-compose stops the DB container mid-test - with the expectation "Ingestion buffers or fails loudly (no silent data loss beyond a defined bounded buffer window); OMS refuses to place orders it cannot durably record rather than trading blind; health dashboard reflects DB-down state immediately." `04-security-program.md` §5.8 rates disk exhaustion (S2) **Critical** because it takes trading down. And `21-database-schema.md` §5.3 states an ordering invariant whose only real proof is a crash test.

Scripted chaos in R0 establishes the baseline behaviour that E45 (Reconciliation, chaos & failover resilience, R4) later extends.

## Scope / Deliverables
Scenarios, each automated in `tests/chaos/storage/` and runnable in the nightly job:

1. **QuestDB down mid-ingest.** Stop the container while fixtures replay. Expect: writer applies backpressure within the bounded buffer, `questdb_write_errors_total` climbs, `storage_tier_health{tier="questdb"}` goes down, `/readyz` reflects it, and on restart the buffered batch flushes exactly once with no duplicate and no missing rows (dedup makes a re-flush safe).
2. **Postgres down.** Expect: the app fails readiness loudly rather than serving; no partial writes; on recovery, UoW transactions resume; a `system_events` row records both transitions.
3. **Disk full on the recording volume.** Fill to <5 % free. Expect: critical event **before** any deletion, recording paused for non-pinned auto-recorded symbols, pinned data untouched, **and the trading path still functional** because it does not share the volume (SR-096) - asserted by exercising a Postgres write while the recording volume is full.
4. **Crash between Parquet write and manifest entry.** SIGKILL the exporter at that exact point. Expect: re-run reconciles to a single manifest entry, zero rows lost, hot partition still present.
5. **Crash between manifest entry and hot-partition drop.** Expect: duplicate data across tiers (harmless, dedup on read), zero rows lost; the router's straddle merge returns no duplicates to the caller.
6. **Export verify mismatch.** Inject a row-count discrepancy. Expect: CRITICAL `system_events`, run aborted, hot data retained, alert delivered, no partition dropped.
7. **Corrupted Parquet file.** Flip a byte. Expect: scrub/read-time checksum detects it, quarantines the file, alerts, and serves no data from it (SR-094).
8. **Two reaper instances racing.** Expect: locking or idempotency prevents double-deletion and double-audit entries.
9. **Clock step backwards during the export window.** Expect: partition selection uses monotonic/exchange time semantics and does not re-export or skip a window.

## Out of scope
- Exchange-side chaos (WS disconnect, 5xx, rate-limit 10018) - E08/E45.
- Host/VM failover and backup restore drills - E43/PRR (this ticket proves the data invariants, not the recovery runbook).
- Network partition between tiers beyond container stop/start.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given each of the nine scenarios
When it runs in the nightly chaos job
Then the expected behaviour above is asserted programmatically, not observed manually, and a failure names the violated invariant

Given scenario 5 (crash after manifest, before drop)
When the system is inspected afterwards
Then rows exist in both tiers and a straddling read returns each row exactly once, proving the "duplicate is harmless, missing is not" design of 21-database-schema.md §5.3

Given scenario 3 (disk full)
When the guard trips
Then the critical alert timestamp precedes every deletion timestamp in the audit log, and a Postgres write succeeds during the event

Given scenario 6 (verify mismatch)
When the run aborts
Then zero QuestDB partitions were dropped and the hot data is fully readable

Given scenario 7 (corrupted file)
When a read touches the quarantined partition
Then it fails loudly with a named error rather than returning truncated or silently wrong results

Given any scenario leaves the system in an inconsistent state
When triaged
Then it is priority/p0 if data is lost and priority/p1 if data is duplicated or unavailable, per the data-loss severity rule
```

## Technical notes / design
Fault injection uses docker-compose container control for stop/start and `SIGKILL` at instrumented breakpoints for the crash scenarios: the exporter exposes test-only hook points (`AFTER_PARQUET_WRITE`, `AFTER_CHECKSUM`, `AFTER_MANIFEST`) that are no-ops unless `CV_ENV=test`, which is how scenarios 4 and 5 hit the exact instruction boundary the §5.3 invariant is written about.

Disk-full scenarios operate on a dedicated small loopback filesystem image mounted at the cold root, never on the CI runner's real volume; the harness refuses to run if the target mount is not that image.

Each scenario is structured as `arrange -> inject -> assert(data) -> assert(signals) -> assert(health) -> recover -> assert(recovery)` and cleans up in a `finally` block, so a failed assertion still leaves the environment reusable.

## Test plan
Implemented with docker-compose container control plus `pumba`-style fault injection for process kills, and a loopback filesystem image of fixed small size for the disk-full scenarios (filling a real volume in CI is not acceptable). Each scenario asserts on three surfaces: the data (row counts, checksums), the observability signals (metrics, `system_events`, audit entries) and the health/readiness endpoints. Every scenario must be **repeatable and self-cleaning** - a chaos test that leaves residue is a flaky test generator.

## Security notes
Scenarios 3, 6, 7 and 8 are direct verifications of security controls SR-096 (disk-budget guard, trading unaffected), SR-094 (checksum manifest, quarantine) and SR-099 (pins honoured, deletions audited, no double-deletion). Findings here are control failures and are copied to E07-X02 and the Security engineer, not merely filed as bugs. The disk-full scenario must never target a shared volume; the harness asserts it is operating on its own loopback image.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - though scenario outputs feed the SCR-142 degraded states reviewed in E07-D02.

## Performance notes
Recovery time is measured, not just correctness: time from container restart to `storage_tier_health` returning ok, and time to drain the buffered batch. Recorded as a baseline for E45's failover budgets.

## Observability
Each scenario asserts the expected signal appears: `system_events` severity and code, the metric that should move, the audit entry that should exist. A scenario that behaves correctly but silently is a **failure** of this suite - silent correct behaviour is indistinguishable from silent failure to an operator.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All nine scenarios automated, green in the nightly job, self-cleaning.
- [ ] Findings filed; P0/P1 resolved or accepted-risk with Owner sign-off.
- [ ] Recovery-time baselines recorded and handed to E45.
- [ ] Security engineer notified of the control-verification results (input to E07-X02).
- [ ] Runbook notes contributed for "QuestDB down", "disk full" and "export verify failed" (feeds E48).
- [ ] QA sign-off contribution recorded on E07-T04 and E07-T05.

- `E07-T04` (exporter/manifest crash points).
- `E02-T08` compose stack for container control.

title: Security: STRIDE threat model for recorder data & storage (Area 8) with abuse cases
body:
## Context
`00-planning-brief.md` makes a STRIDE threat model per epic non-negotiable, and `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.1 requires the kickoff scheduled at Epic DoR. `04-security-program.md` §5.8 already contains **Area 8 - Recorder data & storage (A-10, A-12, A-13)** with six threats (S1 Parquet corruption, S2 disk exhaustion **Critical**, S3 path traversal, S4 export scoping, S5 pinned-data deletion, S6 console exposure). That table is the *planning-level* model; this ticket produces the **implementation-level** model for what E07 actually builds, confirms or refutes the residual-risk ratings against the real design, and hands E07-T05 the constraints it must implement (which is why it blocks T05).

## Scope / Deliverables
- Implementation-level STRIDE model document `docs/security/threat-models/E07-storage.md` covering:

title: Security: verify storage controls SR-047/048/090-099, add SAST rules and a DAST/path-traversal probe
body:
## Context
A control that is specified but never verified is a control that does not exist. `04-security-program.md` SR-150 requires every SR to map to at least one automated test or a scheduled manual procedure, with a traceability table checked at PRR. This ticket closes E07's half of that obligation for the storage-relevant SRs and adds the static/dynamic rules that stop the controls from regressing.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Control verification** - one automated test or a documented procedure per SR:
  | SR | Control | Verification |
  |---|---|---|
  | SR-047 | Loopback/WSL-internal binds only; startup listener self-check | Automated: boot the stack, enumerate listening sockets, assert no non-loopback bind for postgres/questdb/minio; assert the app's own startup self-check refuses to start on a violation |
  | SR-048 | Data-store ports not published to host/tailnet; QuestDB console off/loopback-only | Automated: parse compose files, assert every published port binds 127.0.0.1; probe the QuestDB HTTP console from a non-loopback interface and assert refusal |
  | SR-090/091/092 | Backups cover PG + Parquet + config, encrypted with a key distinct from the runtime KEK, useless without it | Procedure: documented backup of the E07 tiers, decryption attempt without the backup key must fail; recorded in the PRR-lite evidence |
  | SR-093 | Restore drill per release | Procedure: one restore of Postgres + a Parquet partition into a scratch environment; assert the app starts and recorded data reads back |
  | SR-094 | Cold-tier checksum manifest verified on read and by a weekly scrub | Automated: corrupt a file, assert quarantine + alert; assert the weekly scrub job is scheduled and its last-run timestamp is observable |
  | SR-096 | Storage guard: separate volume, 75 % / 90 % thresholds, trading unaffected | Automated (shares E07-Q04 scenario 3): assert alert precedes deletion, recorder pauses, a Postgres write succeeds while the recording volume is full |
  | SR-097 | No filesystem paths in replay/export/read APIs; registry ids only | Automated: path-traversal and symlink-escape matrix against `ColdTierRepository.query` and any endpoint surface reaching it |
  | SR-099 | Retention honours pins, dry-run first, deletions audited | Automated: pinned symbol survives a full cycle; every deletion has exactly one audit entry with symbol/stream/range/bytes |
- **SAST rules** (Semgrep, added to the E03 pipeline): forbid f-string/`%`/`+` construction of SQL in `storage/**`; forbid `os.path.join` with any value derived from a request model in `storage/cold/**`; forbid `open()` on a path not rooted at `CV_COLD_ROOT`; forbid `pickle`/`eval`/`exec` anywhere in `storage/**`; forbid logging of any variable named `dsn`, `password`, `secret`, `token`.
- **DAST probe** (OWASP ZAP job addition, scoped to what exists at R0): path-traversal payloads against any storage-backed read route, plus a check that data-store ports are unreachable through the app's origin.
- **SCA/secrets**: confirm gitleaks covers the new `infra/` and `backend/db/` paths; pin and scan the new dependencies (`pyarrow`, `duckdb`, `asyncpg`, the QuestDB client) with pip-audit, and record an accepted-risk entry for any unavoidable Medium.
- **Traceability table** `docs/security/traceability/E07.md` mapping SR -> test id -> ticket, feeding the PRR checklist.

## Out of scope
- Auth/RBAC control verification - E09/E43.
- Full pen-test - E43 (before Live enablement).
- Key management controls (SR-001..SR-010) - E27; this ticket only asserts no key material reaches E07's tiers.
- Backup *automation* - E43; here the procedure is executed once, manually, and documented.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given the traceability table
When it is reviewed at the R0 PRR-lite
Then every storage-relevant SR listed above has a test id or a dated executed procedure, and none is marked "to be done"

Given the bind assertions
When any compose file is changed to publish a data-store port on 0.0.0.0
Then CI fails, naming SR-047/SR-048

Given the Semgrep rules
When a developer builds SQL by string concatenation anywhere in storage/**
Then the SAST gate fails the PR with a message pointing at the rule and the threat it mitigates

Given the path-traversal matrix
When ../, absolute paths, URL-encoded traversal, symlinked partition directories and unregistered dataset ids are attempted
Then every attempt is refused and no filesystem access occurs outside CV_COLD_ROOT, asserted by an fs-access spy not merely by the returned error

Given an encrypted backup and no backup key
When decryption is attempted
Then it fails, satisfying SR-092, and the attempt is recorded in the drill notes

Given the restore drill
When Postgres and one Parquet partition are restored into a scratch environment
Then the app starts, the restored partition reads back with matching checksums, and the result is recorded for the PRR

Given any Critical or High SAST/SCA finding on the new dependencies
When the gate runs
Then the build fails; Medium findings require a dated accepted-risk entry per the R0 quality gates
```

## Technical notes / design
Bind assertions parse the compose files statically *and* probe the running stack, because a file can be correct while a runtime override is not. The path-traversal matrix asserts at the filesystem layer using an `open()` spy rather than trusting the returned error, since a control that returns 403 after having already stat-ed the target path has still leaked existence.

Semgrep rules are written against the repository's own idioms (they must not fire on SQLAlchemy Core expressions or on parameterised asyncpg calls) and each ships with a matching `*.fixed.py`/`*.bad.py` pair in the rule tests, so a rule that stops matching is itself caught.

The restore drill is scripted end to end (`infra/scripts/restore_drill.sh`) even though it is executed manually in R0, so E43 can promote it to a scheduled job without rewriting it.

## Test plan
Each row of the control table is a test case with an id; automated cases live in `tests/security/storage/` and run in the `security` CI job; procedures are executed once in R0 with dated notes. Negative controls are mandatory: each rule and assertion is demonstrated *failing* on a deliberately introduced violation, then passing after reverting - a green check that has never been seen red is not evidence.

## Security notes
This ticket is the verification layer for the threats modelled in E07-X01 (S1-S6). Findings are triaged with the Security engineer; Critical/High block the epic's DoD. The drill artifacts (backup files, restore notes) contain no production data - fixtures only - and the backup key used in the drill is a throwaway generated for it.

## Accessibility notes
N/A.

## Performance notes
Per-read checksum verification and the weekly scrub have measurable cost; E07-Q03 measures it and this ticket records the accepted trade-off from E07-X01's model. The DAST job runs nightly, not per-PR, to stay inside the pipeline's 15-minute budget (R0 exit criterion 2).

## Observability
Verifies that each control emits evidence: audit entries for deletions and policy changes, `system_events` for quarantine/verify failure, the alert path for the 75 %/90 % thresholds, and an observable last-run timestamp for the weekly scrub. A control with no signal is filed as a defect against the owning ticket.

- [ ] Every listed SR verified by an automated test or a dated executed procedure.
- [ ] Traceability table committed and accepted at PRR-lite.
- [ ] Semgrep rules merged into the E03 pipeline; each demonstrated failing then passing.
- [ ] DAST job addition merged and run once with results triaged.
- [ ] New dependencies scanned; Critical/High zero, Medium accepted-risk entries dated.
- [ ] Restore drill executed and recorded.
- [ ] **Security engineer sign-off comment** on the epic.

- `E07-T05` (the controls must exist to be verified).
- `E03` pipeline for the SAST/DAST/SCA jobs; `E07-Q04` shares the disk-full scenario.
